        ['9'] = [[4, 3, 1, 3, 0, 2, 0, 1, 1, 0, 3, 0, 4, 1, 4, 5, 3, 6, 1, 6, 0, 5]],
    };

    private static readonly char[] Alphabet = [.. Font.Keys];

    // a few dark colors, easy to read on the light background
    private static readonly string[] Colors = ["#1f4e79", "#7b2d26", "#2e6b30", "#5b2c83", "#8a5a00", "#23395d", "#9c2a5b"];

    // RandomNumberGenerator: a "cryptographic" random number generator,
    // unpredictable (unlike Random, whose sequence could be guessed)
    public static string RandomText(int length) =>
        new(Enumerable.Range(0, length).Select(_ => Alphabet[RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(Alphabet.Length)]).ToArray());

    private static double RandomBetween(double min, double max) =>
        min + (max - min) * RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(1_000_001) / 1_000_000.0;

    public static string Svg(string text)
    {
        var svg = new StringBuilder();
        svg.Append($"<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"{Width}\" height=\"{Height}\" viewBox=\"0 0 {Width} {Height}\">");
        svg.Append($"<rect width=\"100%\" height=\"100%\" fill=\"#f5f7fa\"/>");

        // the characters: each one enlarged, tilted, shifted, and each point
        // slightly moved at random
        var step = (Width - 20) / (double)text.Length;
        for (var i = 0; i < text.Length; i++)
        {
            var scale = RandomBetween(4.6, 5.6); // size of a grid unit, in pixels
            var angle = RandomBetween(-0.35, 0.35); // rotation, in radians (about ±20°)
            var cx = 10 + step * (i + 0.5) + RandomBetween(-3, 3); // center of the character
            var cy = Height / 2.0 + RandomBetween(-4, 4);
            var color = Colors[RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(Colors.Length)];
            var d = new StringBuilder();
            foreach (var stroke in Font[text[i]])
            {
                for (var k = 0; k < stroke.Length; k += 2)
                {
                    // grid point, centered on (2, 3), distorted, rotated, placed
                    var x = (stroke[k] - 2 + RandomBetween(-0.2, 0.2)) * scale;
                    var y = (stroke[k + 1] - 3 + RandomBetween(-0.2, 0.2)) * scale;
                    var px = cx + x * Math.Cos(angle) - y * Math.Sin(angle);
                    var py = cy + x * Math.Sin(angle) + y * Math.Cos(angle);
                    d.Append(k == 0 ? 'M' : 'L').Append(Number(px)).Append(' ').Append(Number(py)).Append(' ');
                }
            }
            svg.Append($"<path d=\"{d.ToString().TrimEnd()}\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{color}\" stroke-width=\"{Number(RandomBetween(2.2, 3))}\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"/>");
        }

        // 3 scrambling strokes: curves that cross the image
        for (var n = 0; n < 3; n++)
        {
            var color = Colors[RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(Colors.Length)];
            svg.Append($"<path d=\"M{Number(RandomBetween(0, 20))} {Number(RandomBetween(5, 45))} " +
                       $"C{Number(RandomBetween(30, 60))} {Number(RandomBetween(0, 50))} {Number(RandomBetween(90, 120))} {Number(RandomBetween(0, 50))} " +
                       $"{Number(RandomBetween(130, 150))} {Number(RandomBetween(5, 45))}\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{color}\" stroke-width=\"1.3\"/>");
        }

        svg.Append("</svg>");
        return svg.ToString();
    }

    // a number with a decimal point, whatever the language of the server
    // (in French, ToString() would write "12,5" - unreadable for SVG)
    private static string Number(double value) => value.ToString("0.#", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
}

The file contains two classes: the service class, which is identical to the one in Example 27 except for one safeguard, and the [CaptchaDrawing] class that generates the image, which was already discussed in Example 27 (file [Auth/CaptchaDrawing.cs]). Let’s go over this code:

  • line 44: a CAPTCHA, as received by the page: the identifier, to be placed in a hidden form field, and the image [SVG];
  • lines 49–52: An image is valid for ten minutes, and there is a cap on the number of pending captchas. Each time the login page is displayed, a captcha is added to memory; without a cap, a bot that requested this page millions of times without ever responding would eventually exhaust the server’s memory;
  • line 55: id → (expected answer, expiry date). The pair is a tuple whose elements are named ([Text], [Expires]). The service is a singleton, used by concurrent requests: hence the [ConcurrentDictionary] (see Example 27);
  • lines 57–63: the cleanup, followed by a randomly generated five-character text string, stored under a random identifier ([Guid.NewGuid()], impossible to guess), and displayed;
  • lines 70–77: verification, identical to that in Example 27: the CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases ([TryRemove]), then the system verifies that it has not expired and that the entered text, with spaces removed, is correct, regardless of case. [TryRemove] is atomic: if two requests present the same CAPTCHA at the same time, only one removes it;
  • lines 80–87: Expired captchas are discarded; if the limit is reached, valid captchas are also removed until the count falls below the limit. A [ConcurrentDictionary] can be modified while it is being processed, which is not allowed with a standard [Dictionary] (see [AttemptLimiterService], below). However, it does not preserve the insertion order: the CAPTCHAs removed in this way are not necessarily the oldest ones, whereas the [Map] from the [NestJS] project allowed the oldest ones to be removed first. This situation only occurs in the event of an attack: the approximation is sufficient;
  • line 96: the image drawing. [internal]: the class is only visible within the application itself;
  • lines 104–136: the “font”: for each character, a list of strokes, each stroke being a sequence of (x, y) coordinates in a 4 × 6 grid. The square brackets [[...]] are collection expressions ([C#] 12), a compact notation for arrays;
  • line 139: the usable characters, i.e., the font keys. [..] spreads one collection into another;
  • lines 146–147 and lines 149–150: the randomization uses [RandomNumberGenerator], a cryptographic generator whose outputs are unpredictable;
  • lines 152–194: the image is a [SVG] text, assembled into a [StringBuilder] (a string that is extended without being rewritten each time an element is added). Each character (lines 160–181) becomes a [<path>] path: each point on the grid is slightly shifted, enlarged, rotated, and placed in its position within the image, with a randomly selected color and line thickness. The characters are lines, never text: a bot cannot read them in the image’s code. Three scrambling curves then cross the image (lines 185–190);
  • line 199: the numbers in [SVG] are written with a decimal point. [CultureInfo.InvariantCulture] enforces this notation regardless of the server’s language: in French, [ToString()] would use a comma (see Chapter 5).

docs.title: 11.13.6. Auth/AttemptLimiterService.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/AttemptLimiterService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second line of defense against robots (the first is the captcha): we COUNT
// the attempts, and beyond a threshold we BLOCK for a while.
//
//   - login: after LoginMaxFailures failures (wrong captcha or wrong
//     password) for the same login from the same IP address, this pair
//     is blocked LoginBlockMinutes minutes. The same IP address is also
//     blocked if it accumulates 5 times more failures, all logins combined (a
//     robot that tries thousands of different logins);
//   - account creation: at most RegistrationMaxPerHour accounts created per
//     hour from the same IP address.
//
// Beware in a classroom: all the computers often go out to the Internet
// through the SAME IP address. That is why the login block applies
// first to the (IP, login) pair - a student who mistypes their
// password does not block their neighbors - and why the thresholds are adjustable
// in appsettings.json ("Protection" section).
//
// Singleton service, called by parallel requests: all the
// operations on the counters are done under a lock, which guarantees
// that only one thread at a time reads AND modifies a counter.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
using RdvMedecins.Config;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public class AttemptLimiterService(IOptions<ProtectionOptions> options)
{
    private class Counter
    {
        public int Count; // attempts counted in the current window
        public DateTime Start; // start of the counting window
        public DateTime BlockedUntil; // DateTime.MinValue if not blocked
    }

    private static readonly TimeSpan OneHour = TimeSpan.FromHours(1);

    private readonly Dictionary<string, Counter> counters = [];
    private readonly Lock syncLock = new(); // the Lock type of .NET 9+, made for "lock"

    private readonly int maxLoginFailures = options.Value.LoginMaxFailures;
    private readonly TimeSpan loginBlockDuration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(options.Value.LoginBlockMinutes);
    private readonly int maxRegistrations = options.Value.RegistrationMaxPerHour;

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- login

    // number of remaining block minutes (0 = the attempt is allowed)
    public int LoginBlockMinutes(string ip, string login)
    {
        lock (syncLock)
        {
            return Math.Max(RemainingMinutes(LoginKey(ip, login)), RemainingMinutes(IpKey(ip)));
        }
    }

    public void LoginFailure(string ip, string login)
    {
        lock (syncLock)
        {
            Count(LoginKey(ip, login), maxLoginFailures, loginBlockDuration, loginBlockDuration);
            Count(IpKey(ip), maxLoginFailures * 5, loginBlockDuration, loginBlockDuration);
        }
    }

    // a successful login resets the counter of THIS login
    public void LoginSuccess(string ip, string login)
    {
        lock (syncLock)
        {
            counters.Remove(LoginKey(ip, login));
        }
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

    public int RegistrationBlockMinutes(string ip)
    {
        lock (syncLock)
        {
            return RemainingMinutes($"registration|{ip}");
        }
    }

    // one-hour window; once the quota is reached, blocked until the end of the hour
    public void RegistrationSuccess(string ip)
    {
        lock (syncLock)
        {
            Count($"registration|{ip}", maxRegistrations, OneHour, OneHour);
        }
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- shared mechanics
    // (the private methods are always called under the lock)

    private int RemainingMinutes(string key)
    {
        if (!counters.TryGetValue(key, out var c))
        {
            return 0;
        }
        var remaining = c.BlockedUntil - DateTime.UtcNow;
        return remaining > TimeSpan.Zero ? (int)Math.Ceiling(remaining.TotalMinutes) : 0;
    }

    // counts an attempt; if the threshold is reached within the window, blocks
    private void Count(string key, int max, TimeSpan window, TimeSpan block)
    {
        var now = DateTime.UtcNow;
        Purge(now);
        if (!counters.TryGetValue(key, out var c) || now - c.Start > window)
        {
            c = new Counter { Count = 0, Start = now, BlockedUntil = DateTime.MinValue };
            counters[key] = c;
        }
        c.Count++;
        if (c.Count >= max)
        {
            c.BlockedUntil = now + block;
            c.Count = 0; // after the block, we start again from zero
            c.Start = c.BlockedUntil;
        }
    }

    // we forget the counters that are no longer useful (neither blocked, nor recent)
    private void Purge(DateTime now)
    {
        if (counters.Count < 1000)
        {
            return;
        }
        foreach (var (key, c) in counters.ToList())
        {
            if (c.BlockedUntil < now && now - c.Start > OneHour)
            {
                counters.Remove(key);
            }
        }
    }

    private static string LoginKey(string ip, string login) => $"login|{ip}|{login.Trim().ToLowerInvariant()}";

    private static string IpKey(string ip) => $"ip|{ip}";
}

Compared to Example 27, the limiter protects two operations (the connection and account creation); the connection block applies to the pair (address IP, login), and the thresholds are configurable in [appsettings.json]. Let’s break down this code:

  • line 31: [IOptions<ProtectionOptions>] specifies the section [Protection] of [appsettings.json] (folder [Config]): the number of allowed failed login attempts (5 by default), the lockout duration (15 minutes), and the number of accounts created per hour (10);
  • lines 33–37: a counter: the number of attempts, the start of the counting window, and the end of the lockout ([DateTime.MinValue], the earliest possible date, if there is no lockout). This is a nested, private class: it exists only for this service. It is a class, not a [record] or a structure: a counter read from the dictionary is modified in place;
  • Lines 42–43: an ordinary [Dictionary], protected by a lock (see Example 27). A [ConcurrentDictionary] would not be sufficient: counting an attempt involves reading a counter, modifying it, and possibly replacing it, and this entire sequence of operations must be executed without another request interrupting it. Each public method therefore performs its task within a [lock (syncLock)] block;
  • lines 45–47: the thresholds, read once and for all. The main constructor’s parameter can be used to initialize the fields;
  • lines 52–56: the remaining lockout time for a connection attempt: the longer of the two possible lockout periods, that of the pair (address IP, login) and that of the address IP alone;
  • lines 60–65: A failed attempt is counted twice. For the pair (address IP, login): five failed attempts with the same login block that login, from that address only. For the address IP alone, with a threshold five times higher: a bot that tries a large number of different logins is also blocked. In a classroom, all computers often connect to the Internet via the same address, IP: a student who enters the wrong password should not block their neighbors, hence the blocking by pair;
  • lines 70–74: a successful login resets the counter for that specific login (not the one for the address IP);
  • lines 80–84 and lines 89–93: For account creation, only successful attempts are counted: a maximum of ten accounts per hour from the same address IP. Once the quota is reached, the address is blocked for one hour;
  • lines 100–107: the remaining minutes of the block, rounded up to the next whole number ([Math.Ceiling]): it shows “1 minute” rather than “0 minutes” when there are 20 seconds remaining. These private methods do not acquire the lock: they are always called by a public method that already holds it;
  • lines 111–125: counting. An unknown key, or one whose counting window has expired, starts with a new counter. When the threshold is reached, the key is locked, and counting will resume from zero at the end of the lock;
  • lines 130–140: cleaning up counters that are no longer needed (neither locked nor recent), performed only when the dictionary exceeds 1,000 entries. We iterate through a copy of the entries ([ToList()]): a [Dictionary] cannot be modified while it is being iterated over;
  • lines 145–147: generating the dictionary keys. Spaces are removed from the login and it is converted to lowercase: [Admin] and [admin] share the same counter; a bot cannot bypass the lock by changing the case.

docs.title: 11.13.7. Auth/RegistrationPassService.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Auth/RegistrationPassService.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The "pass" of account creation.
//
// To open the "Create a patient account" page, you must first have
// copied the captcha of the authentication page (see
// RegistrationController, POST /register/access). The server then issues
// a pass:
//   - a random identifier, stored in an HttpOnly cookie;
//   - valid for 15 minutes (the time to fill in the form, even if it takes
//     several attempts after input errors);
//   - consumed as soon as an account is created: ONE solved captcha = ONE account at
//     most. A robot cannot create accounts in series.
//
// Without a valid pass, GET and POST /register send back to the
// authentication page: typing the /register URL directly does not allow
// bypassing the captcha.
//
// Like the captcha, the passes live in the memory of the process.
// =========================================================================

using System.Collections.Concurrent;

namespace RdvMedecins.Auth;

public class RegistrationPassService
{
    public const string Cookie = "rdvmedecins_registration";

    private static readonly TimeSpan Lifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15);
    private const int MaxPasses = 10_000;

    // id -> expiry date
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime> passes = new();

    // issues a new pass; returns its identifier
    public string Issue()
    {
        Purge();
        var id = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();
        passes[id] = DateTime.UtcNow + Lifetime;
        return id;
    }

    // true if [id] is an existing, non-expired pass
    public bool IsValid(string? id) =>
        id is not null && passes.TryGetValue(id, out var expires) && expires > DateTime.UtcNow;

    // the pass has been used: we forget it
    public void Consume(string? id)
    {
        if (id is not null)
        {
            passes.TryRemove(id, out _);
        }
    }

    // the cookie is sent by the browser only to the /register... addresses
    public static CookieOptions GetCookieOptions() => new()
    {
        HttpOnly = true,
        SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax,
        MaxAge = Lifetime,
        Path = "/register",
    };

    private void Purge()
    {
        var now = DateTime.UtcNow;
        foreach (var (id, expires) in passes)
        {
            if (expires <= now || passes.Count >= MaxPasses)
            {
                passes.TryRemove(id, out _);
            }
        }
    }
}

You can create a customer account from the login page, provided you have solved the CAPTCHA. The registration form is displayed and submitted via subsequent requests: these requests must know that a previous request successfully solved the CAPTCHA. This is the role of the pass, issued and verified by [RegistrationController] (documented in the controllers):

  • line 29: the name of the cookie that carries the pass;
  • lines 31–35: a pass is valid for fifteen minutes; pending passes are kept in memory, like captchas, with the same time limit;
  • lines 38–43: A pass is a random identifier, stored along with its expiration date; the controller places it in a cookie;
  • lines 47–48: the registration form is displayed—and accepted—only with a valid pass. Verification does not consume the pass ([TryGetValue], not [TryRemove]): the user can resubmit the form multiple times if they made input errors;
  • lines 51–55: Creating an account consumes the pass: solving a CAPTCHA entitles the user to one account, and no more;
  • lines 60–65: cookie options. [new()] creates an object of the type declared by the method ([CookieOptions]). The option [Path = "/register"] limits the sending of the cookie to URL values that begin with [/register]: other requests do not carry it unnecessarily;
  • lines 68–75: the cleanup process, identical to that of the CAPTCHA.

docs.title: 11.13.8. Controllers/AuthController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/AuthController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The NON-protected routes of the login:
//   GET  /        redirects to the home page of the role (or to /login)
//   GET  /login   displays the login form (with its captcha)
//   POST /login   checks attempt limit, captcha, login / password
//   POST /logout  clears the token cookie
//
// An MVC controller inherits from Controller and returns an IActionResult:
// View(...) to display a page, Redirect(...) to redirect...
// [HttpGet("login")] / [HttpPost("login")]: "attribute routing",
// the equivalent of @Get('login') / @Post('login').
//
// Protection against robots, in this order:
//   1. too many recent failures for this login from this IP address?
//      -> immediate refusal, without even looking at the password;
//   2. wrong answer to the captcha? -> refusal (counted as a failure);
//   3. only then, verification of the password.
// We NEVER check the password of an attempt refused at steps
// 1 or 2: a robot can therefore learn nothing by insisting.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Models;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class AuthController(
    AuthService authService,
    CaptchaService captchaService,
    AttemptLimiterService limiter) : Controller
{
    // the home page of each role, right after logging in
    public static string HomePage(Role role) => role == Role.USER ? "/my-area" : "/schedule";

    [HttpGet("/")]
    public IActionResult Home()
    {
        // User: the user of the request, rebuilt from the token by
        // the authentication middleware (see Auth/ConnectedUser.cs)
        var user = User.CurrentUser();
        return Redirect(user is not null ? HomePage(user.Role) : "/login");
    }

    // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the login
    // field (used right after the creation of an account, see RegistrationController)
    [HttpGet("login")]
    public IActionResult ShowLogin(string? login)
    {
        // already logged in (token still valid): straight to the home page
        var user = User.CurrentUser();
        if (user is not null)
        {
            return Redirect(HomePage(user.Role));
        }
        return Form(login is null ? "" : login[..Math.Min(login.Length, 30)]);
    }

    // the parameters of the action are filled with the form fields of the
    // same name (model binding); [FromForm] specifies that they are looked for in
    // the body of the POST request
    [HttpPost("login")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> LogIn(
        [FromForm] string? login,
        [FromForm] string? password,
        [FromForm] string? captchaId,
        [FromForm] string? captcha)
    {
        login = (login ?? "").Trim();
        password ??= "";
        var ip = IpAddress(HttpContext);

        // 1. too many recent failures?
        var minutes = limiter.LoginBlockMinutes(ip, login);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return Form(login, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }

        // 2. the captcha
        if (!captchaService.Verify(captchaId, captcha))
        {
            limiter.LoginFailure(ip, login);
            return Form(login, "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA");
        }

        // 3. the password
        var user = login != "" && password != "" ? await authService.ValidateUserAsync(login, password) : null;
        if (user is null)
        {
            limiter.LoginFailure(ip, login);
            return Form(login, "LOGIN.ERROR");
        }

        limiter.LoginSuccess(ip, login);
        authService.SetToken(Response, user);
        return Redirect(HomePage(user.Role));
    }

    // logout with a POST (and not with a simple GET link): a third-party site cannot
    // log the user out without their knowledge (see SameSite, AuthService)
    [HttpPost("logout")]
    public IActionResult LogOut()
    {
        AuthService.ClearToken(Response);
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

    // the IP address of the visitor. Behind a reverse proxy (nginx...), the
    // UseForwardedHeaders middleware would have to be enabled to get the one of the
    // visitor and not the one of the proxy.
    public static string IpAddress(HttpContext http) => http.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString() ?? "unknown";

    // the form, always with a NEW captcha (each image is used only once)
    private ViewResult Form(string login, string? error = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? errorParams = null) =>
        View("Login", new LoginModel
        {
            PageTitle = "LOGIN.TITLE",
            Login = login, // we redisplay the typed login, never the password
            Captcha = captchaService.Generate(),
            Error = error,
            ErrorParams = errorParams,
        });
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 31–34: the controller receives the three services it needs. No attributes [[Authorize]]: its pages are accessible without being logged in;
  • line 37: The home page depends on the role: “My area” for a patient, the calendar for others;
  • lines 39–45: The site root redirects to the role-specific home page or to the login page. The authentication middleware runs for all requests, whether protected or not: if the cookie contains a valid token, [User] is populated, even here. The [NestJS] project, on the other hand, was supposed to verify the token itself (method [readToken]), since the token check is not applied to this route;
  • lines 50–59: a user who is already logged in is redirected to their home page. The optional parameter [login], which comes from URL (see Example 07), pre-fills the field after an account is created. [login[..n]] (range operator) preserves the first [n] characters: its length is limited to 30, because data from the request is never used without taking precautions;
  • Lines 65–70: the fields of the login form (see Example 11), including the CAPTCHA ID, transmitted via a hidden field, and the user’s input. All are declared as [string?]: a missing field yields [null], and it is the action that determines what to do with it;
  • lines 72–74: A missing login becomes an empty string; [password ??= ""] only affects the empty string if [password] is [null];
  • lines 77–80: 1. A blocked pair isn’t even processed: neither the CAPTCHA nor the password is checked. The error is a translation key with one parameter: the number of minutes to wait;
  • lines 84–87: 2. the CAPTCHA. An incorrect CAPTCHA counts as a failure (see example 27);
  • lines 91–95: 3. Only then is the password checked. An empty username or password is not subjected to the computationally expensive [bcrypt] calculation. Unknown username or incorrect password: the same deliberately vague message (see Example 25), and another failure;
  • lines 98–100: success: counter reset to zero, token stored in the cookie, redirection to the role’s home page;
  • lines 105–109: logout, using POST (see Example 25);
  • line 115: the client’s address IP, provided by the network connection ([RemoteIpAddress], which may be [null], hence [?.] and [??]). The method is public and static: [RegistrationController] and [PatientAreaController] also use it for the limiter. Behind an intermediary server (a reverse proxy such as [nginx]), this address would be that of the proxy: the comment specifies the middleware to enable in this case;
  • lines 118–125: the login page, always with a new CAPTCHA: each image is used only once. Its template, [LoginModel] (folder [Models]), contains the page title (a translation key), the entered username (never the password), the CAPTCHA, and any error messages, along with the translation key and parameters. [error] and [errorParams] are optional parameters: they default to [null] when the call does not provide them.

docs.title: 11.14. The Web Layer: Shared Services
docs.text: Before we get to the controllers and views, here’s what they have in common: translation, the parent class for views, flash messages, the exception filter, the cache for lists of doctors and clients, the preparation of forms to be re-displayed, and a few utility functions. All these files are in the [Web] folder. It brings together most of the techniques from Examples 16 through 24.

docs.title: 11.14.1. Web/Translator.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Translator.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// French / English translation of the interface.
//
// The dictionaries are the SAME files as those of the NestJS project
// (i18n/fr.json, i18n/en.json), read only once at startup. A Razor
// view translates a key with @T("KEY") (see Web/ViewPage.cs).
//
// ASP.NET Core also offers its own system (IStringLocalizer and
// .resx files); keeping the JSON files allows sharing the
// dictionaries with the other versions of the application.
//
// THE CURRENT LANGUAGE: it is the localization middleware of ASP.NET Core
// (UseRequestLocalization, see Program.cs) that determines it on each request,
// from a cookie, and stores it in CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.
// =========================================================================

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public partial class Translator
{
    public static readonly string[] Languages = ["fr", "en"];
    public const string DefaultLanguage = "en";

    // language -> (full key "LOGIN.TITLE" -> text)
    private readonly Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>> dictionaries = [];

    public Translator(IWebHostEnvironment environment)
    {
        foreach (var language in Languages)
        {
            var path = Path.Combine(environment.ContentRootPath, "i18n", $"{language}.json");
            using var document = JsonDocument.Parse(File.ReadAllText(path));
            var dictionary = new Dictionary<string, string>();
            Flatten(document.RootElement, "", dictionary);
            dictionaries[language] = dictionary;
        }
    }

    // the language of the current request: "fr" or "en"
    public static string CurrentLanguage()
    {
        var language = CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.TwoLetterISOLanguageName;
        return Languages.Contains(language) ? language : DefaultLanguage;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Translate("DOCTORS.ADDED", { ["name"] = "Marie PELISSIER" })
    //   -> looks up "DOCTORS.ADDED" in the dictionary of the current language,
    //      and replaces {name} with its value. A key missing from the requested
    //      language is looked up in the default language; missing everywhere, the
    //      key itself is displayed (an omission is thus spotted immediately).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public string Translate(string? key, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? messageParams = null)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(key))
        {
            return "";
        }
        var text = dictionaries[CurrentLanguage()].GetValueOrDefault(key)
                    ?? dictionaries[DefaultLanguage].GetValueOrDefault(key)
                    ?? key;
        if (messageParams is null || messageParams.Count == 0)
        {
            return text;
        }
        return Parameter().Replace(text, m => messageParams.TryGetValue(m.Groups[1].Value, out var value) ? value : m.Value);
    }

    // { "LOGIN": { "TITLE": "Login" } } -> { "LOGIN.TITLE": "Login" }
    private static void Flatten(JsonElement node, string prefix, Dictionary<string, string> result)
    {
        foreach (var property in node.EnumerateObject())
        {
            var key = prefix == "" ? property.Name : $"{prefix}.{property.Name}";
            if (property.Value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object)
            {
                Flatten(property.Value, key, result);
            }
            else
            {
                result[key] = property.Value.GetString() ?? "";
            }
        }
    }

    // the {name} regular expression, compiled once and for all by the
    // C# compiler ([GeneratedRegex] "source generator")
    [GeneratedRegex(@"\{(\w+)\}")]
    private static partial Regex Parameter();
}

This is the translation service from Example 22, saved as a singleton in [Program.cs]: The dictionaries [i18n/fr.json] and [i18n/en.json] are the same files as those in version [NestJS], read only once at startup. There is only one difference:

  • lines 65–67: a key missing from the French dictionary is looked up in the English dictionary ([DefaultLanguage]); if it is missing everywhere, the key itself is displayed. The two [??] operators are chained together: the first value that is not [null] is taken.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/ViewPage.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The parent class of ALL the Razor views of the application (see
// Views/_ViewImports.cshtml: @inherits ViewPage<TModel>).
//
// A .cshtml view is compiled into a C# class, child of RazorPage<TModel>.
// By inserting our own class, we give all the views what they
// need, whatever the page:
//   - @T("KEY")          : the translation of a key (the equivalent of the
//                          Handlebars helper {{t 'KEY'}});
//   - Language           : "fr" or "en";
//   - CurrentUser        : the connected user, for the navigation bar;
//   - FlashMessage       : the flash message of the request;
//   - CurrentPath        : the requested URL (active menu of the navigation bar).
// In NestJS, this information went through res.locals.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Razor;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Razor.Internal;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public abstract class ViewPage<TModel> : RazorPage<TModel>
{
    // [RazorInject]: the property is filled by dependency injection,
    // as the @inject directive would do in a view
    [RazorInject]
    public Translator Translator { get; set; } = null!;

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // @T("BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT", ("time", "8:00 - 8:20"))
    // The parameters are "tuples" (name, value): a compact syntax
    // to write pairs of values.
    // The returned text is then ESCAPED by Razor (< becomes <): a name
    // typed by a user cannot therefore inject HTML into the page.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public string T(string? key, params (string Name, object? Value)[] messageParams) =>
        Translator.Translate(key, messageParams.ToDictionary(p => p.Name, p => p.Value?.ToString() ?? ""));

    // the same, with the parameters of a flash message or of a BusinessException
    public string T(string? key, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? messageParams) => Translator.Translate(key, messageParams);

    public string Language => Translator.CurrentLanguage();

    public ViewUser? CurrentUser => ViewUser.Of(Context.User.CurrentUser());

    public FlashMessage? FlashMessage => Flash.Read(Context);

    public string CurrentPath => Context.Request.Path.Value ?? "/";

    // "active" if the current page is under this path (menu of the navigation bar)
    public string Active(string prefix) => CurrentPath.StartsWith(prefix, StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "active" : "";
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the connected user, as the views see them
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public record ViewUser(string Login, string Name, string Role, bool IsAdmin, bool IsPatient)
{
    public static ViewUser? Of(ConnectedUser? u) =>
        u is null
            ? null
            : new ViewUser(
                u.Login,
                u.Name,
                u.Role.ToString(),
                IsAdmin: u.Role == Entities.Role.ADMIN, // ADMIN: Doctors / Patients menus
                IsPatient: u.Role == Entities.Role.USER); // USER: My area menu
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 25: the parent class of all views, designated by the [@inherits] directive of [Views/_ViewImports.cshtml], as in Example 22. It serves the same purpose as [res.locals] in version [NestJS]: it provides each view with what all pages need;
  • lines 29–30: the translation service, injected into the property (see Example 22);
  • lines 39–40: the [T] method from Example 22: [@T("KEY", ("name", value))]. The rendered text is escaped by [Razor]: a name entered by a user cannot inject HTML into the page;
  • line 43: a second version of [T], which directly accepts a dictionary: this is the form in which the parameters of a flash message or a [BusinessException] are passed. Two methods with the same name, which differ in their parameters, are overloaded methods: the compiler selects the correct one based on the arguments;
  • line 45: the current language ([fr] or [en]), for the page’s [lang] attribute and the FR / EN;
  • Line 47: the logged-in user, for the navigation bar, or [null] if there is none. [Context.User] is the request user, reconstructed from the token JWT by the authentication middleware (see Chapter 8); the method [CurrentUser()] (file [Auth/ConnectedUser.cs]) extracts the account from it. In version [NestJS], an interceptor was required to copy [req.user] into [res.locals] after the guards; here, the property is calculated when the view reads it, well after authentication;
  • line 49: the request’s flash message (see [Web/Flash.cs], below);
  • lines 51–54: the path of the requested URL, and the method that returns [active] if the current page is under a given path: this is how the navigation bar highlights the current menu item, for example [@Active("/my-")] (see Example 16). [StringComparison.Ordinal] compares characters one by one, regardless of language;
  • lines 60–70: the logged-in user as seen by the views: login, name, role, and two Booleans, [IsAdmin] and [IsPatient], which prevent the views from comparing roles. The static method [Of] creates this object from the logged-in account, or returns [null]; the operator [? :] chooses between the two. The arguments [IsAdmin:] and [IsPatient:] are named: the parameter name is written before the value, which makes the call more readable.

docs.title: 11.14.3. Web/Flash.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Flash.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The "flash" messages: a message to display ONCE, on the
// NEXT page. It is the natural complement of the "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern
// used by all the forms of the application: a successful POST does not
// build a page, it redirects (302) to a GET page - if
// the user then reloads this page (F5), the browser does not send
// the form a second time. The message, however, must survive the
// redirection.
//
// In NestJS, we had programmed it ourselves (a short-lived cookie).
// ASP.NET Core MVC offers it as standard: it is TempData. A value stored
// in TempData is kept (by default in an encrypted cookie) until
// a following request READS it; it is then erased.
// =========================================================================

using System.Text.Json;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public enum FlashType
{
    Success, // Bootstrap alert-success class: at the top of the page
    Danger, // an error: at the bottom of the page (see Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml)
}

// Key: translation key; Params: its parameters ({name}, {login}...)
public record FlashMessage(FlashType Type, string Key, Dictionary<string, string>? Params = null);

public static class Flash
{
    private const string Key = "flash";

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // puts a flash message, which will be displayed by the NEXT page.
    // We go through ITempDataDictionaryFactory (and not through the TempData property
    // of a controller) to be able to put a message from ANYWHERE:
    // a controller, but also the JWT authentication (expired session, see
    // Auth/JwtAuthentication.cs), which runs outside MVC.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static void Put(HttpContext http, FlashType type, string key, Dictionary<string, string>? messageParams = null)
    {
        var tempData = TempDataOf(http);
        // TempData can only keep simple values: we store the
        // message as JSON text
        tempData[Key] = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new FlashMessage(type, key, messageParams));
        // Save(): writes the cookie right away (outside MVC, nobody
        // would do it for us)
        tempData.Save();
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // reads (and therefore erases) the flash message of the request. The page may
    // ask for it several times (the success message is displayed at the top, the error
    // one at the bottom): we keep it in HttpContext.Items, a dictionary
    // that lives for the time of the request.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static FlashMessage? Read(HttpContext http)
    {
        if (http.Items.TryGetValue(Key, out var alreadyRead))
        {
            return alreadyRead as FlashMessage;
        }
        FlashMessage? message = null;
        if (TempDataOf(http)[Key] is string json)
        {
            try
            {
                message = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<FlashMessage>(json);
            }
            catch (JsonException)
            {
                // unreadable message: we ignore it
            }
        }
        http.Items[Key] = message;
        return message;
    }

    private static ITempDataDictionary TempDataOf(HttpContext http) =>
        http.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<ITempDataDictionaryFactory>().GetTempData(http);
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 23–26: the two types of messages: a success message, displayed at the top of the page (partial view [_Flash.cshtml]), and an error message, displayed at the bottom (partial view [_Errors.cshtml]);
  • line 30: a flash message consists of a translation key and its parameters, not pre-translated text; it will be translated on the next page, in that page’s language;
  • line 32: a static class that contains only functions (see [Web/Utils.cs]). [TempData] (see Example 20) does most of the work: it stores the value in an encrypted cookie until the next request and deletes it once it has been read. In the [NestJS] version, this short-lived cookie had been programmed manually;
  • lines 43–51: sets a message. [TempData] can only store simple values (text, numbers): the message is stored as text JSON ([JsonSerializer.Serialize]). The method receives [HttpContext] and not the [TempData] property of a controller: it can therefore be called from outside MVC, for example by the authentication JWT, when a session has expired (see [Auth/JwtAuthentication.cs]). Outside of MVC, no one would save [TempData] at the end of the request: [Save()] writes the cookie immediately;
  • Lines 60–79: reads the request message. Reading [TempData] marks it as consumed; however, the page requests it twice (at the top for a success, at the bottom for an error). The first call therefore stores the result in [HttpContext.Items], the request-scope dictionary (see Chapter 6), where the second call retrieves it (line 62);
  • lines 71–73: [Deserialize] reconstructs the object [FlashMessage] from JSON. An unreadable text should not cause the page to fail: the exception is caught and the message is ignored;
  • lines 82–83: the [TempData] from the request, obtained from the [ITempDataDictionaryFactory] service. [RequestServices] provides access to dependency injection from a static class, which cannot receive services via its constructor.

docs.title: 11.14.4. Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// How the errors become HTML pages. Three mechanisms
// of ASP.NET Core share the work (see Program.cs):
//
//   1. this MVC exception filter: an InvalidSessionException (account
//      deleted since the login) -> back to the login page;
//   2. UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/error/{0}"): any 400,
//      403 or 404 response WITHOUT content (return BadRequest(), insufficient role, unknown
//      page...) is replaced by the corresponding error page;
//   3. UseExceptionHandler("/error/500"): any other exception (a real
//      anomaly) is written to the server log, and the user
//      sees the 500 error page - never the call stack.
//
// In NestJS, a single filter (HtmlExceptionFilter) did all this.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Filters;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public class HtmlExceptionFilter : IExceptionFilter
{
    public void OnException(ExceptionContext context)
    {
        if (context.Exception is InvalidSessionException)
        {
            AuthService.ClearToken(context.HttpContext.Response);
            Flash.Put(context.HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED");
            context.Result = new RedirectResult("/login");
            context.ExceptionHandled = true;
        }
        // the other exceptions are not handled here: they go up
        // to UseExceptionHandler (500 page)
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Line 25: An exception filter, as in Example 24, added as a global filter in [Program.cs]. In version [NestJS], a single filter converted all errors into HTML pages. Here, the work is shared between two middleware components of the framework, configured in [Program.cs]: [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute] replaces 400, 403, and 404 responses with no content with the corresponding error page (see Example 24), and [UseExceptionHandler("/error/500")] intercepts all other exceptions: the error is logged in the server log, along with its call stack, but the user sees only the 500 error page, as these details could assist an attacker;
  • lines 29–34: the filter handles only one scenario: the logged-in user’s account has been deleted since they logged in, even though their token is still valid (see [Web/Utils.cs], below). The token cookie is cleared, a “session expired” flash message is displayed, and the user is redirected to the login page. The other exceptions are not marked as handled: they continue on to [UseExceptionHandler].

docs.title: 11.14.5. Web/ApplicationModel.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/ApplicationModel.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The cache / facade already present in the JSON server (equivalent of the
// [ApplicationModel] class of the Spring project): the lists of doctors and
// clients are read once at startup, then served from memory.
//
// These lists can CHANGE (the ADMIN adds, edits, deletes
// doctors and clients): each write therefore goes through this facade,
// which reloads the list concerned right after. That is the whole point of a
// SINGLE entry point to the business layer: the rule "write =>
// cache reload" is written only here.
//
// Important difference with NestJS: the LIFETIME of the objects.
//   - In NestJS, all the services were singletons.
//   - Here, the DbContext - hence the repositories and the business layer - lives
//     for the time of ONE HTTP request ("scoped" lifetime, see Program.cs).
//   - But the cache must survive from one request to the next.
// We therefore separate the two roles:
//   - ListCache (singleton): the two lists, and nothing else;
//   - ApplicationModel (scoped): the facade, which uses the business layer of
//     the current request and updates the cache.
// =========================================================================

using RdvMedecins.Domain;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Business;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The cache itself, shared by all the requests (singleton).
//
// ASP.NET Core processes the requests IN PARALLEL, on several threads (Node,
// for its part, has only one). We therefore never modify a list in place: we
// REPLACE it entirely with a new one. Swapping a reference is atomic;
// "volatile" guarantees that all the threads immediately see the new list.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class ListCache
{
    private volatile IReadOnlyList<Doctor> doctors = [];
    private volatile IReadOnlyList<Client> clients = [];

    public IReadOnlyList<Doctor> Doctors
    {
        get => doctors;
        set => doctors = value;
    }

    public IReadOnlyList<Client> Clients
    {
        get => clients;
        set => clients = value;
    }
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The facade (scoped): same contract as the business layer (IBusiness).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class ApplicationModel(IBusiness business, ListCache cache) : IBusiness
{
    // initial loading of the two lists, called once at startup
    // (see Program.cs). If the database is unreachable, the exception stops the
    // server with an explicit message - clearer than starting "empty".
    public async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        await ReloadDoctorsAsync();
        await ReloadClientsAsync();
    }

    private async Task ReloadDoctorsAsync() => cache.Doctors = await business.GetAllDoctorsAsync();

    private async Task ReloadClientsAsync() => cache.Clients = await business.GetAllClientsAsync();

    // ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

    public Task<List<Doctor>> GetAllDoctorsAsync() => Task.FromResult(cache.Doctors.ToList());

    public Task<List<Client>> GetAllClientsAsync() => Task.FromResult(cache.Clients.ToList());

    // the doctor whose user account is [userId] - used to preselect,
    // for a logged-in doctor, their own schedule
    public Doctor? GetDoctorByUserId(int userId) => cache.Doctors.FirstOrDefault(d => d.UserId == userId);

    // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    public Task<List<Slot>> GetAllSlotsAsync(int doctorId) => business.GetAllSlotsAsync(doctorId);

    public Task<List<Appointment>> GetDoctorDayAppointmentsAsync(int doctorId, DateOnly day) => business.GetDoctorDayAppointmentsAsync(doctorId, day);

    public Task<Client?> GetClientByIdAsync(int id) => business.GetClientByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<Doctor?> GetDoctorByIdAsync(int id) => business.GetDoctorByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<Appointment?> GetAppointmentByIdAsync(int id) => business.GetAppointmentByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<Slot?> GetSlotByIdAsync(int id) => business.GetSlotByIdAsync(id);

    public Task<DoctorDaySchedule?> GetDoctorDayScheduleAsync(int doctorId, DateOnly day) =>
        business.GetDoctorDayScheduleAsync(doctorId, day);

    // no cache here: it is the most recent data that matters (a patient
    // who has just edited or deleted their account)
    public Task<Client?> GetClientByUserIdAsync(int userId) => business.GetClientByUserIdAsync(userId);

    public Task<List<Appointment>> GetClientUpcomingAppointmentsAsync(int clientId) => business.GetClientUpcomingAppointmentsAsync(clientId);

    public Task<Appointment> AddAppointmentAsync(DateOnly day, Slot slot, Client client) => business.AddAppointmentAsync(day, slot, client);

    public Task DeleteAppointmentAsync(Appointment appointment) => business.DeleteAppointmentAsync(appointment);

    // ------------------------------------------------ writes => reload

    public async Task<Doctor> AddDoctorAsync(PersonData data)
    {
        var doctor = await business.AddDoctorAsync(data);
        await ReloadDoctorsAsync();
        return doctor;
    }

    public async Task<Doctor> EditDoctorAsync(int id, PersonData data)
    {
        var doctor = await business.EditDoctorAsync(id, data);
        await ReloadDoctorsAsync();
        return doctor;
    }

    public async Task DeleteDoctorAsync(int id)
    {
        await business.DeleteDoctorAsync(id);
        await ReloadDoctorsAsync();
    }

    public async Task<Client> AddClientAsync(PersonData data)
    {
        var client = await business.AddClientAsync(data);
        await ReloadClientsAsync();
        return client;
    }

    public async Task<Client> EditClientAsync(int id, PersonData data)
    {
        var client = await business.EditClientAsync(id, data);
        await ReloadClientsAsync();
        return client;
    }

    public async Task DeleteClientAsync(int id)
    {
        await business.DeleteClientAsync(id);
        await ReloadClientsAsync();
    }
}

Lists of doctors and clients are displayed on almost every page (calendar drop-down lists, administration pages). Rather than retrieving them from the database with every request, they are kept in memory: this is application-scope data (see Chapter 6). Version [NestJS] assigned this role to a single service, which was a singleton like all [NestJS] services. In [ASP.NET Core], this is impossible: the business layer uses [DbContext], which exists only for the duration of a request ([Scoped] service; see Chapter 9), and a singleton cannot accept a [Scoped] service. We therefore separate the two roles into two classes.

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 39: the cache itself, registered as a singleton ([AddSingleton<ListCache>()] within [Program.cs]). It contains only the two lists;
  • Lines 41–42: [ASP.NET Core] processes requests in parallel across multiple threads ([threads]), whereas [Node.js] has only one. A shared list must therefore never be modified while another request is iterating through it. The rule we’ve chosen is simple: we never modify a list; we replace it with a new one. Replacing a reference is done in a single operation, and the keyword [volatile] ensures that all threads immediately see the new list. [IReadOnlyList] allows only reading: the compiler prohibits adding or removing an element;
  • Line 60: the facade, registered as service [Scoped] ([AddScoped<ApplicationModel>()]). It receives the business layer for the current request and the shared cache. It implements the same [IBusiness] interface as the business layer: for the controllers, it is the business layer, and it is the only one they receive;
  • Lines 65–68: the initial loading of the two lists. It is called once, by [Program.cs], before the server starts. A [Scoped] service exists only within a scope: [Program.cs] creates one for this purpose ([CreateScope]). If the database is inaccessible, the exception terminates the application with an explicit message, which is better than starting a server with empty lists;
  • lines 71–73: reloading a list: the entire list is read from the database and replaces the one in the cache;
  • lines 77–79: the lists are served from memory. The [IBusiness] interface declares an asynchronous method: [Task.FromResult] creates a task that has already completed, which carries the result. [ToList()] returns a copy of the list: the caller can modify it without affecting the cache;
  • line 83: the doctor associated with an account, retrieved from the cache: a logged-in doctor immediately sees their own schedule;
  • lines 87–110: the other requests are forwarded as-is to the business layer;
  • line 104: a client associated with an account is intentionally not looked up in the cache; a patient who has just modified or deleted their account must be displayed as they appear in the database;
  • lines 114–151: Any write operation involving doctors or clients is followed by a refresh of the relevant list. Since this service is the only entry point for controllers to the business layer, the rule “write = cache refresh” is implemented only here, and the cache cannot become stale. If the business layer rejects the operation ([BusinessException]), the exception terminates the method before the cache is reloaded, as this step is no longer necessary.

docs.title: 11.14.6. Web/Validation.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Validation.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What is needed to REDISPLAY a refused form: the input errors
// field by field, and the fields to outline in red.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ModelBinding;
using RdvMedecins.Models;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public static class Validation
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // ModelState (filled by MVC when binding the form) -> the
    // field -> message key dictionary, keeping only the first
    // message of each field: { "LastName": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", ... }
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static Dictionary<string, string> ErrorsOf(ModelStateDictionary modelState)
    {
        var errors = new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        foreach (var (field, entry) in modelState)
        {
            if (entry.Errors.Count > 0)
            {
                var message = entry.Errors[0].ErrorMessage;
                errors[field] = string.IsNullOrEmpty(message) ? "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM" : message;
            }
        }
        return errors;
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // the form fields concerned by each "input" business error
    // (a duplicate): they are outlined in red, the message being at the bottom of the page
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static readonly Dictionary<string, string[]> BusinessErrorFields = new()
    {
        ["ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"] = ["login"],
        ["ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS"] = ["firstName", "lastName"],
        ["ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS"] = ["firstName", "lastName"],
    };

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // prepares a form model for its (re)display:
    //   errors       : message under each field refused by the validation
    //   error        : THE error message of the page, displayed at the bottom of the page;
    //                  by default "The form contains errors." if there
    //                  are field errors
    //   otherFields  : fields to outline in red WITHOUT their own message
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static T Prepare<T>(
        T model,
        Dictionary<string, string>? errors = null,
        string? error = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? otherFields = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? errorParams = null) where T : FormView
    {
        model.Errors = errors ?? new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        model.InvalidFields = new HashSet<string>(model.Errors.Keys.Concat(otherFields ?? []), StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        model.Error = error ?? (model.Errors.Count > 0 ? "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM" : null);
        model.ErrorParams = errorParams;
        return model;
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 20–31: Convert [ModelState] (see examples 07 and 19) into a simple “field → message key” dictionary. Only the first message for each field is retained: a single message is displayed under the field. The dictionary ignores uppercase letters (line 22): [ModelState] names the fields based on the properties ([LastName], [Login]), whereas the views request them based on the HTML fields ([lastName], [login]);
  • lines 27–28: As a precaution, an error without a message (such as one caused by an exception) is assigned the generic message [ERRORS.INVALID_FORM];
  • lines 38–42: certain errors in the business layer relate to specific fields: a username that is already taken, or a doctor or client with the same name. These fields will be highlighted in red, with the message displayed at the bottom of the page. The syntax [["key"] = value] populates the dictionary as soon as it is created;
  • lines 53–64: prepares a form template for display or redisply: the messages below the fields ([Errors]), the fields to be framed in red ([InvalidFields]: those with a message, plus the [otherFields] fields, line 61), the message at the bottom of the page, and its parameters. In the absence of an explicit message, field errors result in the message “The form contains errors” (line 62). The method is generic: the constraint [where T : FormView] (line 58) accepts any model derived from [FormView] (see [Models/ViewModels.cs]), and it returns the model with its exact type, ready to be passed to [View]. The parameters have default values ([= null]): the caller provides only those it needs.
