docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Web/Utils.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Small utility functions of the web layer:
//   - Labels   : "Mme Alice DURAND";
//   - WebDates : dates "yyyy-MM-dd", times "8:05", days "Wednesday 23 September 2026";
//   - Input    : reading of a positive integer sent by the browser;
//   - Patient  : the patient (Client entity) of the connected user.
//
// "static" classes: they only contain functions, we never create
// an object of these classes.
// =========================================================================

using System.Globalization;
using System.Security.Claims;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;

namespace RdvMedecins.Web;

public static class Labels
{
    // "Mme Alice DURAND"
    public static string Label(Person p) => $"{p.Title} {p.FirstName} {p.LastName}";
}

public static class WebDates
{
    // the format of the dates in the URLs and in the <input type="date"> field
    public const string IsoFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd";

    // true if [day] is a date that exists in the yyyy-MM-dd format
    // ("2026-02-30" is refused)
    public static bool IsValidDate(string? text, out DateOnly day) =>
        DateOnly.TryParseExact(text, IsoFormat, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None, out day);

    public static string Iso(DateOnly day) => day.ToString(IsoFormat, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

    // "8:05" rather than "8:5"
    public static string FormatTime(int h, int m) => $"{h}:{m:00}";

    public static string Time(Slot s) => $"{FormatTime(s.StartHour, s.StartMinute)} - {FormatTime(s.EndHour, s.EndMinute)}";

    // "mercredi 23 septembre 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026", depending on the
    // language of the request (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, set by the
    // localization middleware - see Program.cs)
    public static string FormatDay(DateOnly day) =>
        day.ToString("dddd d MMMM yyyy", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture);
}

public static class Input
{
    // "3" -> 3 ; "", "abc", "-2", null -> null
    public static int? PositiveInteger(string? value) =>
        int.TryParse(value, NumberStyles.None, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var n) && n > 0 ? n : null;
}

public static class Patient
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // The patient (Client entity) that corresponds to the connected user.
    //
    // The JWT token only contains the id of the ACCOUNT (users.id). For a
    // USER role, we find the corresponding client thanks to the clients.user column.
    //
    // If there is none, the account has been deleted since the
    // login while its token is still valid: we treat it as an
    // expired session (see InvalidSessionException).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    public static async Task<Client> ConnectedPatientAsync(ApplicationModel application, ClaimsPrincipal user)
    {
        var currentUser = user.CurrentUser() ?? throw new InvalidSessionException();
        return await application.GetClientByUserIdAsync(currentUser.UserId) ?? throw new InvalidSessionException();
    }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 24: the name of a doctor or a client: “Mme Alice DURAND.” The parameter is of type [Person], the parent class of entities [Doctor] and [Client]: the same function is used for both;
  • line 30: the date format in the URL entities and in the [<input type="date">] field;
  • Lines 34–35: true if the text is a date in the [yyyy-MM-dd] format that exists; [2026-02-30] is rejected (see Example 12). The result is returned in the parameter [out day]. [CultureInfo.InvariantCulture] makes the analysis independent of the query language;
  • line 37: the reverse operation: a date to the text [yyyy-MM-dd];
  • lines 40–42: a time in the [8:05] format (the [00] format requires two digits for the minutes), and the time of a time slot: [8:00 - 8:20];
  • lines 47–48: a day written out in full, according to the request’s locale, as determined by the localization middleware (see Example 22): “mercredi 23 septembre 2026” or “Wednesday 23 September 2026”;
  • lines 54–55: an identifier sent by the browser (in the URL or a form field): a strictly positive integer, or [null]. [NumberStyles.None] accepts only digits: no signs, spaces, or thousands separators. The controller simply needs to test [null];
  • lines 70–73: the patient (entity [Client]) associated with the logged-in user. The token JWT contains only the account ID; we look for the customer associated with that account. If it no longer exists, it means the account has been deleted since the user logged in: [InvalidSessionException] will be processed by the [HtmlExceptionFilter] filter described above, which redirects to the login page. [?? throw] throws an exception when the value on the left is [null] (see Chapter 9).

docs.title: 11.15. Form and View Templates
docs.text: Two types of classes transport data between the browser, controllers, and views: forms, populated by the model binding based on what the browser sends, and view models, prepared by controllers for the views. The former correspond to the DTO objects in version [NestJS], while the latter correspond to the objects passed to [res.render].

docs.title: 11.15.1. Models/Forms.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Models/Forms.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The fields of the "person" forms and their constraints. Three
// forms share the same identity fields (title, first name, last name):
//
//   PersonFields                  title, first name, last name
//    ├─ PersonForm                + OPTIONAL login / password, version
//    │                              (the ADMIN adds or edits a doctor / client)
//    ├─ RegistrationForm          + REQUIRED login / password / confirmation
//    │                              (a patient creates their account)
//    └─ MyAccountForm             + login, optional new password,
//                                   REQUIRED CURRENT password, version
//                                   (a patient edits their account)
//
// MODEL BINDING: when a controller action receives
// a parameter of one of these classes, ASP.NET Core MVC creates the object and
// fills each property with the form field of the same name (regardless
// of case: the "lastName" field fills the LastName property).
//
// VALIDATION: right after, MVC checks the [Required],
// [MaxLength]... attributes (standard namespace System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations,
// the equivalent of class-validator) and stores the errors in ModelState.
// The controller only has to test ModelState.IsValid.
//
// The error messages are translation KEYS (see i18n/*.json).
//
// INPUT CLEANING (the equivalent of the @Transform of class-transformer):
//   - MVC already turns an empty field into null;
//   - the setters below remove the superfluous spaces and put the
//     login in lower case. A password, however, is not "cleaned" (the
//     spaces may be part of it).
// All the properties are "nullable" (string?): a field may always be
// missing from what the browser sends; it is [Required] that requires it.
// =========================================================================

using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;

namespace RdvMedecins.Models;

public static class InputRules
{
    public static readonly string[] Titles = ["Mr", "Mme", "Melle"];

    // login: lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore - 30 characters at most
    public const string LoginFormat = "^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$";

    // minimum length of a password CHOSEN by a patient
    public const int PasswordMin = 6;

    // "  dupont " -> "dupont" ; "   " -> null
    public static string? Clean(string? value) => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value) ? null : value.Trim();
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "home-made" validation attribute: the value must belong to a list.
// It is enough to inherit from ValidationAttribute and write IsValid.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public class OneOfAttribute(params string[] values) : ValidationAttribute
{
    // null is accepted here: it is the role of [Required] to require it
    public override bool IsValid(object? value) => value is null || values.Contains(value as string);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
public class PersonFields
{
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")]
    [OneOf("Mr", "Mme", "Melle", ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")]
    public string? Title { get; set; }

    // maximum lengths = those of the SQL columns (VARCHAR(20))
    private string? firstName;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? FirstName
    {
        get => firstName;
        set => firstName = InputRules.Clean(value);
    }

    private string? lastName;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED")]
    [MaxLength(20, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? LastName
    {
        get => lastName;
        set => lastName = InputRules.Clean(value);
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
public class PersonForm : PersonFields
{
    private string? login;

    // optional (see PersonData, Business/IBusiness.cs)
    [RegularExpression(InputRules.LoginFormat, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = InputRules.Clean(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

    // optional; 72 characters at most (beyond that, bcrypt ignores the rest)
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    // hidden field of the edit form (optimistic lock).
    // int?: a missing or empty field gives null; a text that is not a
    // number gives a binding error (see Program.cs, ModelBindingMessageProvider)
    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration of a patient
public class RegistrationForm : PersonFields
{
    private string? login;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED")]
    [RegularExpression(InputRules.LoginFormat, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = InputRules.Clean(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED")]
    [MinLength(InputRules.PasswordMin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT")]
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED")]
    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage my account"
public class MyAccountForm : PersonFields
{
    private string? login;

    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED")]
    [RegularExpression(InputRules.LoginFormat, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")]
    public string? Login
    {
        get => login;
        set => login = InputRules.Clean(value)?.ToLowerInvariant();
    }

    // optional: empty = password unchanged
    [MinLength(InputRules.PasswordMin, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT")]
    [MaxLength(72, ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }

    // the CURRENT password, required for any modification of the account
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED")]
    public string? CurrentPassword { get; set; }

    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

Let's discuss this code:

  • line 43: possible titles;
  • line 46: the format of a username, described by a regular expression: 1 to 30 characters consisting of lowercase letters, digits, a period, a hyphen, and an underscore;
  • line 49: the minimum length of a password chosen by a patient. This is a constant ([const]), so it can be used as an argument for an attribute, such as [[MinLength(InputRules.PasswordMin)]] below;
  • line 52: cleaning up an entry: leading and trailing spaces are removed, and a field consisting solely of spaces becomes [null], meaning it is invalid;
  • lines 59–62: a validation attribute we wrote: the value must appear in a list. All we need to do is derive it from [ValidationAttribute] and redefine [IsValid]. [null] is accepted: it is the role of [[Required]] to reject a missing field. We use it under the name [[OneOf]]: by convention, the suffix [Attribute] can be omitted;
  • Line 66: the identity fields, common to all three forms. All properties are of type [string?]: a field may always be missing in the data sent by the browser, and it is [[Required]] that requires it. Error messages are translation keys (see Example 22);
  • Lines 68–70: the title, which is required and selected from the list. The values are repeated in [[OneOf(...)]]: an attribute’s argument must be known at compile time, which is not the case for the array [InputRules.Titles] (a [static readonly] field, created at runtime);
  • lines 73–80 and lines 83–90: the first name and last name, which are required and may be up to 20 characters long (the width of the SQL columns). These properties have a body: their value is stored in a private field, and [set] cleans it up as it passes through. Since the model binding affects the properties before validation, it is the cleaned-up value that is validated. This is equivalent to the [@Transform] in version [NestJS]; [ASP.NET Core MVC] already automatically converts an empty field to [null];
  • line 95: the ADMIN form, for adding or editing a doctor or a client. The class inherits the identity fields and their validation attributes;
  • lines 97–104: the login, which is optional here but must be in the correct format if present (line 100); it is sanitized and converted to lowercase. [?.] calls [ToLowerInvariant] only if the value is not [null];
  • lines 108–109: the password, also optional, with a maximum of 72 characters: the [bcrypt] algorithm, which encrypts it, ignores any characters following it. A password is not sanitized: spaces are included as part of it;
  • line 114: the record’s version, in a hidden field of the update form (optimistic lock; see Example 28). A missing or empty field results in [null]; text that is not a number produces a binding error, whose message is configured in [Program.cs] (see Example 19);
  • Line 118: A patient creates an account: username, password (6 to 72 characters, line 131), and confirmation (lines 135–136) are required. Verifying that the password matches its confirmation involves two fields: this is checked by the validator ([Controllers/RegistrationController.cs]);
  • Line 140: A patient modifying their account. The new password is optional (line 153): if left blank, the password remains unchanged; its confirmation (line 157) is therefore not required here. The current password, however, is required for any changes (lines 160–161), and the record version is stored in a hidden field (line 163).

docs.title: 11.15.2. Models/ViewModels.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Models/ViewModels.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The "view models": what each controller passes to
// its view (return View("...", model)), in a TYPED C# class. In a
// Razor view, @model ScheduleModel declares the type of the model: the compiler
// then checks each @Model.Xxx of the view - a typo is a
// compilation error, and not an empty area in the page.
//
// Rule already followed with Handlebars: no logic in the views. The
// controllers prepare data ALREADY formatted ("Mme Marie
// PELISSIER", "8:00 - 8:20", Selected = true...) and already filtered according to
// the role of the user; the views merely place them in the HTML.
// =========================================================================

namespace RdvMedecins.Models;

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// what ALL the pages have in common, read by the layout
// (Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
public abstract class ViewModel
{
    // translation key of the page title (<title>)
    public string PageTitle { get; set; } = "APP.TITLE";

    // THE error message of the page, displayed at the bottom of the page
    // (see Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml); null = no error
    public string? Error { get; set; }

    public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? ErrorParams { get; set; }
}

// an option of a drop-down list (doctor, patient)
public record OptionView(int Id, string Label, bool Selected);

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ login
public class LoginModel : ViewModel
{
    public string Login { get; set; } = "";
    public required Auth.Captcha Captcha { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ schedule
public class ScheduleRowView
{
    public int SlotId { get; init; }
    public string Time { get; init; } = ""; // "8:00 - 8:20"
    public bool Free { get; init; }
    public string? Patient { get; init; } // name displayed for a booked slot; null = "Booked"
    public bool Mine { get; init; } // the appointment of the connected patient
    public bool Bookable { get; init; } // display the "Book" button?
    public string BookUrl { get; init; } = "";
    public int? AppointmentId { get; init; } // filled only if the "Cancel" button is displayed
}

public record ScheduleView(string Doctor, string Day, List<ScheduleRowView> Rows);

public class BookingView
{
    public int SlotId { get; init; }
    public string Time { get; init; } = "";
    // ADMIN / DOCTOR: the list of the patients to choose from
    public List<OptionView> Clients { get; init; } = [];
    // USER: the patient is themselves
    public string? Patient { get; init; }
}

public class ScheduleModel : ViewModel
{
    public List<OptionView> Doctors { get; set; } = [];
    public int? DoctorId { get; set; }
    public string Day { get; set; } = ""; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
    public ScheduleView? Schedule { get; set; }
    public BookingView? Booking { get; set; }
    public string BackUrl { get; set; } = "/schedule"; // the displayed schedule, without booking dialog
    // patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the message that explains
    // why there is no "Book" button
    public string? Info { get; set; }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ "person" forms

// the values displayed in the form fields (never the password)
public class PersonValues
{
    public string Title { get; set; } = "Mr";
    public string FirstName { get; set; } = "";
    public string LastName { get; set; } = "";
    public string Login { get; set; } = "";
    public int? Version { get; set; }
}

// what the common partial _PersonFields.cshtml uses (title, first name, last name)
public abstract class FormView : ViewModel
{
    public PersonValues Values { get; set; } = new();

    // field -> key of the message displayed UNDER this field (input error)
    public Dictionary<string, string> Errors { get; set; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    // fields to outline in red (Bootstrap is-invalid class): those that have
    // a message, plus possibly others (duplicate first + last name, login taken...)
    public HashSet<string> InvalidFields { get; set; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    public string? ErrorOf(string field) => Errors.GetValueOrDefault(field);

    public string InvalidClass(string field) => InvalidFields.Contains(field) ? "is-invalid" : "";

    public IEnumerable<(string Value, bool Selected)> Titles =>
        InputRules.Titles.Select(t => (t, t == Values.Title));
}

public class PersonFormModel : FormView
{
    public bool Creating { get; set; } // true: add; false: edit
    public string Action { get; set; } = ""; // URL of the POST
    public string ListUrl { get; set; } = "";
}

public class RegistrationModel : FormView
{
    public int PasswordMin => InputRules.PasswordMin;
}

public class MyAccountModel : FormView
{
    public int PasswordMin => InputRules.PasswordMin;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ doctor / client lists

// the translation keys specific to each type of person
public record PersonKeys(
    string Title, // "Doctors"
    string Add, // "Add a doctor"
    string Edit, // "Edit a doctor"
    string Empty, // "No doctors."
    string ConfirmDelete, // "Delete this doctor, their time slots and their user account?"
    string Added, // "Doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
    string Edited,
    string Deleted);

public record PersonView(string Title, string FirstName, string LastName, string Login, string EditUrl, string DeleteUrl);

public class PersonListModel : ViewModel
{
    public required PersonKeys Keys { get; set; }
    public string AddUrl { get; set; } = "";
    public List<PersonView> Persons { get; set; } = [];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient area
public record AppointmentView(int Id, string Day, string Time, string Doctor, string ScheduleUrl);

public class AreaModel : ViewModel
{
    public string Patient { get; set; } = "";
    public List<AppointmentView> Appointments { get; set; } = [];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ error page
public class ErrorModel : ViewModel
{
    public int Code { get; set; }
    public string Message { get; set; } = "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR";
}

The view templates follow the rule already applied with [Handlebars]: no logic in the views. The controllers prepare data that is already formatted (“Mme Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; the views simply place this data into the HTML. Each view declares the type of its template ([@model ScheduleModel], see Example 13): the compiler checks each [@Model.Xxx], and a typo results in a compilation error.

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 22–31: what all pages have in common, as read by the [_Layout.cshtml] template: the translation key for the page title (line 25), and the page’s error message, displayed at the bottom, along with its parameters. The class is abstract: each page has its own template, which derives from it;
  • line 35: an option from a drop-down list (a doctor, a patient), already marked as selected or unselected (see Example 18);
  • lines 38–41: the login page: the username already entered and the CAPTCHA to be displayed. The keyword [required] requires the person creating the object to assign a value to the property; failing to do so results in a compilation error;
  • lines 45–54: a calendar entry, i.e., a time slot. The controller has already determined everything: whether the patient’s name is displayed (a patient cannot see the names of others), whether the “Book” button is displayed, and whether the “Cancel” button is displayed ([AppointmentId] is set). The properties [init] can only be assigned a value when the object is created;
  • Line 57: A doctor's schedule for a single day: the doctor's name, the day spelled out in full, and the lines;
  • Lines 59–66: The appointment window: the list of patients for ADMIN and the doctors, or just the name of the logged-in patient;
  • lines 69–79: the calendar page: the list of doctors, the selected doctor and day, the calendar ([null] as long as no doctor is selected), the booking window (if present), the calendar URL without this window (line 76), and the message explaining to a patient why they cannot book an appointment;
  • lines 85–91: the values displayed in the fields of a “person” form, never the password: a password is not sent back to the browser;
  • line 95: the parent class of the templates for the three “person” forms, the one required by [Validation.Prepare]: the field values, the messages below the fields (line 100), and the fields to be highlighted in red (line 104). A [HashSet] is a set: each element appears only once, and the membership test is fast;
  • Lines 106–108: two methods for views: a field’s message (or [null]), and the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid], which frames a field in red. Views are named, for example, [@Model.InvalidClass("login")];
  • lines 110–111: the options in the title list, with the selected option marked (see Example 18). Each option is a tuple [(Value, Selected)];
  • lines 114–118: the ADMIN form, used for adding and modifying entries (see Example 28): the mode, the form submission URL, and the list URL for the back button;
  • lines 121–128: the registration and account management forms; they pass the minimum password length to the view, which is used as the [{min}] parameter for the field’s error message and, for registration, for the help text;
  • lines 134–142: the doctor and client management pages are the same views; only their text differs. This [record] contains the translation keys specific to each type of person;
  • lines 144–150: a row in the list of doctors or clients, with the addresses of its Edit and Delete buttons, and the template for the list page;
  • lines 154–159: the patient’s area: their name and upcoming appointments, each with a link to the daily calendar;
  • lines 163–166: the error page: the code HTTP and the message key, which by default is that of a server error.

docs.title: 11.16. The Web Layer: Controllers
docs.text: Controllers are the visible part of the web layer: each one receives requests from a group of pages, reads their parameters, queries the business layer (always through the [ApplicationModel] service), then selects a view and passes it a typed model, or redirects the request. All POST forms follow the Post/Redirect/Get pattern (see Example 20); all messages are translation keys, translated by the view. The login controller, [AuthController], was discussed with authentication.

docs.title: 11.16.1. Controllers/LanguageController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/LanguageController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two FR / EN buttons of the navigation
// bar. Non-protected route: it must be possible to change language before
// logging in.
//
// The choice is stored in THE cookie of the localization middleware
// of ASP.NET Core (CookieRequestCultureProvider, see Program.cs): on each
// following request, this middleware reads it back and sets the language of the request
// (CultureInfo.CurrentCulture / CurrentUICulture). Then we go back to the
// page we came from.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class LanguageController : Controller
{
    [HttpGet("language/{language}")]
    public IActionResult Change(string language)
    {
        if (!Translator.Languages.Contains(language))
        {
            return NotFound(); // -> 404 error page (see Program.cs)
        }
        Response.Cookies.Append(
            CookieRequestCultureProvider.DefaultCookieName,
            // cookie value: "c=en|uic=en" (language of the formats, language of the texts)
            CookieRequestCultureProvider.MakeCookieValue(new RequestCulture(language)),
            new CookieOptions { MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromDays(365), SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, HttpOnly = true, Path = "/" });
        return Redirect(OriginPage());
    }

    // the previous page, according to the HTTP "Referer" header sent by the
    // browser. We only keep its path (/schedule?...): redirecting to a
    // full address supplied by the request would allow sending
    // the user to another site (so-called "open redirect" flaw).
    private string OriginPage()
    {
        var referer = Request.Headers.Referer.ToString();
        if (!Uri.TryCreate(referer, UriKind.Absolute, out var url))
        {
            return "/";
        }
        return url.AbsolutePath.StartsWith("/language/", StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "/" : url.PathAndQuery;
    }
}

This is, except for one line, the controller from Example 22: same route [/language/{language}], same localization middleware cookie, same return to the original page via the header [Referer]. Two clarifications:

  • line 34: the option [Path = "/"] makes the cookie valid for all addresses on the site, regardless of the page from which the language was changed;
  • line 49: if the original page is itself a [/language/...] page, the user is redirected to the site’s root rather than back to that page, which would cause the browser to go in a loop.

docs.title: 11.16.2. Controllers/ScheduleController.cs
docs.text: The application’s main page and the most feature-rich controller. Let’s break it down section by section.

docs.title: 11.16.2.1. The URL files on the page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/ScheduleController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The schedule page: choice of a doctor and a day, schedule of this
// doctor on that day, booking and cancellation of appointments.
//
//   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23               the page
//   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7        the same page, with
//                                                          the booking dialog
//                                                          of slot 7 open
//   POST /schedule/book                                    creates an appointment
//   POST /schedule/cancel                                  cancels an appointment
//
// The whole page is described by its URL: it can be reloaded, bookmarked,
// and the browser's "Back" button used - without a single line
// of JavaScript.
//
// What each one sees and can do:
//
//   | role          | booked slot displayed             | Book               | Cancel  |
//   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
//   | ADMIN, DOCTOR | name of the patient               | for a patient      | yes     |
//   |               |                                   | chosen in a list   |         |
//   | USER (patient)| "Booked", or THEIR name if it is  | for themselves, if | no (*)  |
//   |               | their own appointment             | they have no       |         |
//   |               |                                   | upcoming appt.     |         |
//
//   (*) the patient cancels their appointment from their "My area" page.
//
// CONFIDENTIALITY: for a patient, the name of the OTHER patients is not
// simply hidden by the view - it is never placed in the model
// passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
// not even hidden (a simple "View page source" would otherwise reveal it).
//
// No booking in the past: the "Book" button only appears
// for today and the following days (and the business layer would refuse it
// anyway).
//
// [Authorize] on the class: all the actions require a logged-in
// user (the equivalent of @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)). [Authorize(Roles =
// "...")] on an action additionally requires one of the listed roles (RolesGuard +
// @Roles). Without a valid token: back to /login; insufficient role: 403 page.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Business;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize]
[Route("schedule")]
public class ScheduleController(ApplicationModel application) : Controller
{
    // what the controller knows about the user, to decide what to display
    private record Rights(
        bool Manager, // ADMIN or DOCTOR
        Client? Patient, // the connected client (USER role), otherwise null
        bool PatientCanBook); // USER without an upcoming appointment
  • Lines 7–12: the page’s routes. Note that the booking window is not opened by [JavaScript]: it is a parameter of URL ([book=7]) that instructs the server to render the page with the window open. The “Book” button is therefore simply a link. The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, bookmark it, or use the browser’s “Back” button;
  • lines 18–28: what each role sees and can do. This table is the page’s “specification”: the rest of the controller implements it;
  • lines 30–33: the privacy rule, which we’ll come back to: the names of other patients are not hidden by the view; they are never sent to the browser;
  • lines 55–57: [[Authorize]] on the class: all actions require a logged-in user, regardless of their role (see Example 25). [[Route("schedule")]] is the prefix for all routes in the controller (see Example 02). The controller receives the [ApplicationModel] service via injection (see Example 06) through its main constructor: the parameters written in parentheses after the class name are accessible in all of its methods;
  • lines 60–63: what the controller knows about the logged-in user, calculated once per request (see [RightsAsync], below). A private [record], declared inside the class: it is used only by that class. [Manager] is true for an ADMIN or a DOCTOR; [Patient] is populated only for a client (role USER).

docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /schedule
    // The URL parameters are read raw (Request.Query), to distinguish
    // an ABSENT parameter from an EMPTY one (?doctorId=).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Show()
    {
        string? error = null;
        var user = User.CurrentUser()!;
        var rights = await RightsAsync(user);

        // the day: the one of the URL if it is valid, otherwise today
        var day = Dates.Today();
        if (Request.Query.TryGetValue("day", out var rawDay))
        {
            if (WebDates.IsValidDate(rawDay, out var requestedDay))
            {
                day = requestedDay;
            }
            else
            {
                error = "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE";
            }
        }
        var dayBookable = day >= Dates.Today();

        // the doctor: the one of the URL; failing that, for a logged-in doctor, themselves
        var doctorId = Input.PositiveInteger(Request.Query["doctorId"]);
        if (!Request.Query.ContainsKey("doctorId") && user.Role == Role.DOCTOR)
        {
            doctorId = application.GetDoctorByUserId(user.UserId)?.Id;
        }

        var doctors = (await application.GetAllDoctorsAsync())
            .Select(d => Option(d, d.Id == doctorId))
            .ToList();

        // the schedule, if a doctor is chosen (and the date valid)
        ScheduleView? schedule = null;
        if (doctorId is int id && error is null)
        {
            var doctorSchedule = await application.GetDoctorDayScheduleAsync(id, day);
            if (doctorSchedule is null)
            {
                error = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND";
            }
            else
            {
                var rows = doctorSchedule.DoctorDaySlots.Select(dds =>
                {
                    var (slot, appointment) = (dds.Slot, dds.Appointment);
                    var free = appointment is null;
                    // the appointment of the connected patient?
                    var mine = appointment is not null && rights.Patient is not null && appointment.ClientId == rights.Patient.Id;
                    return new ScheduleRowView
                    {
                        SlotId = slot.Id,
                        Time = WebDates.Time(slot),
                        Free = free,
                        // THE confidentiality point: a patient only receives the name of
                        // THEIR appointment; for the others, null (the view displays "Booked")
                        Patient = appointment is not null && (rights.Manager || mine) ? Labels.Label(appointment.Client) : null,
                        Mine = mine,
                        Bookable = free && dayBookable && (rights.Manager || rights.PatientCanBook),
                        BookUrl = ScheduleUrl(id, day, slot.Id),
                        AppointmentId = appointment is not null && rights.Manager ? appointment.Id : null,
                    };
                }).ToList();
                schedule = new ScheduleView(Labels.Label(doctorSchedule.Doctor), WebDates.Iso(day), rows);
            }
        }
  • Lines 6–7: the route [GET /schedule] (controller prefix, followed by an empty string). The action has no parameters: it automatically reads URL as [Request.Query] (see Example 05). The model binding would convert a [int? doctorId] parameter to [null] whether it is missing or empty; however, these two cases must be distinguished (see below);
  • Lines 10–11: the logged-in user and their permissions. [CurrentUser()] is an extension method (see Example 06) defined in [Auth/ConnectedUser.cs]: it reads the token’s claims and converts them into a typed object. [!] informs the compiler that the result is not [null]: this is certain, since [[Authorize]] has filtered out unauthenticated requests;
  • lines 14–26: the requested day, if valid; today otherwise. [TryGetValue] returns [false] if the parameter [day] is missing: in that case, it returns today, without a message. If present but invalid ([day=2026-02-30]), it generates an error message. Reservations can only be made starting today ([dayBookable]);
  • lines 29–32: the requested doctor. [Input.PositiveInteger] (folder [Web]) returns a strictly positive integer, or [null] if the value is missing, empty, or invalid. If the [doctorId] parameter is missing from URL, a logged-in doctor sees their own schedule: this is their home page. If it is empty ([doctorId=], the “-- choose a doctor --” option in the list), no schedule is displayed;
  • lines 35–37: the options in the doctors’ drop-down list, read from the cache of [ApplicationModel]; the option for the requested doctor is selected (see the [Option] function at the end of the file and Example 18);
  • lines 40–46: The schedule is calculated only if a doctor is selected and the date is valid. [doctorId is int id] checks that the value (of type [int?]) is not [null], and stores its value in a new variable [id], of type [int]. An unknown doctor ID triggers a message, not an error page;
  • lines 50–56: The schedule calculated by the business layer (a [DoctorDaySchedule] object from the [Domain] folder) is converted into array elements, one per time slot. [var (slot, appointment) = ...] breaks down a value pair into two variables. [mine] determines whether the appointment belongs to the logged-in patient;
  • Lines 58–59: The view receives only data that has already been formatted ([8:00 - 8:20]); it no longer has anything to calculate;
  • line 63: the application’s privacy control. The patient’s name is included in the model only for an administrator or for the patient whose appointment it is. For everyone else, the model contains [null], and the view displays “Booked.” The name is not simply hidden by the view: it is never sent to the browser, and “View Page Source” would not reveal it;
  • lines 65–67: what the view must display, as determined by the controller: the “Book” button (available time slot, date not past, and user authorized to reserve), its link (the page’s URL, with [book]), and the “Cancel” button ([AppointmentId] is populated only for an administrator). The view does not make any decisions: it follows these instructions;
  • line 70: the complete schedule: the doctor, the day, the rows.

docs.title: 11.16.2.4. POST /schedule/book
docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /schedule/book   fields: doctorId, day, slotId, clientId
    //
    // For a patient (USER), the clientId field is IGNORED: they always book
    // for themselves. Trusting a field sent by the
    // browser would allow a crafty patient to book in someone else's name.
    //
    // "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern: whatever the result, we do not
    // build a page here - we put a flash message and redirect
    // to the schedule (see Web/Flash.cs).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("book")]
    [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN,DOCTOR,USER")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Book(
        [FromForm] string? doctorId,
        [FromForm] string? day,
        [FromForm] string? slotId,
        [FromForm] string? clientId)
    {
        if (!ReadScheduleRequest(doctorId, day, out var docId, out var requestedDay)
            || Input.PositiveInteger(slotId) is not int sltId)
        {
            return BadRequest(); // -> "invalid request" page (see Program.cs)
        }

        Client? client;
        if (User.IsInRole(nameof(Role.USER)))
        {
            client = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        }
        else
        {
            if (Input.PositiveInteger(clientId) is not int cliId)
            {
                // no patient chosen: we reopen the booking dialog
                Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT");
                return Redirect(ScheduleUrl(docId, requestedDay, sltId));
            }
            client = await application.GetClientByIdAsync(cliId);
        }

        var slot = await application.GetSlotByIdAsync(sltId);
        if (client is null)
        {
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else if (slot is null || slot.DoctorId != docId)
        {
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            try
            {
                // the rules (not in the past, a single upcoming appointment per
                // patient, free slot) are checked by the business layer
                await application.AddAppointmentAsync(requestedDay, slot, client);
                Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, "SCHEDULE.BOOKED");
            }
            // "when": an exception filter. Same rule, but a message in the 2nd
            // person when it is the patient themselves who books ("You
            // already have..." rather than "This patient...")
            catch (BusinessException e) when (e.Key == "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT" && User.IsInRole(nameof(Role.USER)))
            {
                Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO");
            }
            // any other BusinessException becomes a flash message; the other
            // exceptions (real anomalies) are not caught: 500 page
            catch (BusinessException e)
            {
                Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, e.Key, new Dictionary<string, string>(e.Params));
            }
        }
        return Redirect(ScheduleUrl(docId, requestedDay));
    }
  • Lines 12–13: [[Authorize(Roles = ...)]] on the action is added to the class’s [[Authorize]]: all three roles can make reservations (see Example 26). Here, this attribute imposes no further restrictions; it documents the rule and would protect it if a fourth role were to appear;
  • lines 15–18: the fields in the reservation window form (see Example 11). They are received as strings and then carefully converted;
  • lines 20–23: the doctor and the day are hidden fields in the form; they allow the user to return to the displayed calendar. If they are invalid, the request did not originate from our page: it was manually crafted. [BadRequest()] returns a 400 response with no content, which the [UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute] middleware transforms into an error page (see Example 24). [is not int sltId] is the opposite of [is int]: true if the value is [null]; otherwise, [sltId] receives the value;
  • Lines 27–29: For a patient, the [clientId] field is ignored—the system always makes the reservation for the patient itself. Relying on this field, which is sent by the browser, would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name. [Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync] (folder [Web]) identifies the client using the token; [nameof(Role.USER)] is the string ["USER"], verified by the compiler;
  • Lines 33–39: A manager who has not selected a patient is redirected to the booking window (URL with [book]), accompanied by a pop-up error message. [Flash.Put] (folder [Web]) stores the message in [TempData] (see Example 20);
  • lines 42–49: the patient must exist, and the time slot must exist and belong to the doctor in the calendar: you cannot book a time slot belonging to one doctor for another;
  • lines 57–58: The business rules (not in the past, slot available, only one upcoming appointment per patient) are verified by the business logic layer, which raises a [BusinessException] in case of rejection;
  • Lines 63–65: [when] adds a condition to [catch]: it is an exception filter [C#]. This block only catches the [BusinessException] if the condition is true: for a patient, the message “this patient already has an appointment” is replaced by a second-person message. Otherwise, the exception proceeds to the next [catch];
  • lines 69–71: any other [BusinessException] becomes a flash message, along with its key and parameters ([e.Params] is a read-only dictionary: a copy is made of it, of the type expected by [Flash.Put]). The other exceptions are not caught: these are true errors, which result in a 500 error page;
  • Line 74: the PRG schema: regardless of the result, a flash message is displayed and the user is redirected to the calendar, which will display the message. In version [NestJS], a utility function handled this business error conversion; here, the two [catch] blocks are sufficient.

docs.text:
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /schedule/cancel   fields: appointmentId, doctorId, day
    // (a patient cancels THEIR appointment from "My area", not from here)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("cancel")]
    [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN,DOCTOR")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Cancel([FromForm] string? appointmentId, [FromForm] string? doctorId, [FromForm] string? day)
    {
        if (!ReadScheduleRequest(doctorId, day, out var docId, out var requestedDay)
            || Input.PositiveInteger(appointmentId) is not int id)
        {
            return BadRequest();
        }
        var appointment = await application.GetAppointmentByIdAsync(id);
        if (appointment is null)
        {
            // already cancelled (by someone else, or double click)
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            await application.DeleteAppointmentAsync(appointment);
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, "SCHEDULE.CANCELLED");
        }
        return Redirect(ScheduleUrl(docId, requestedDay));
    }
  • lines 5–7: Cancellation is restricted to administrators; a patient cancels their appointment from “My area” (see [PatientAreaController]). A patient who sends this request would receive a 403 page;
  • Lines 9–12: The same checks as for the reservation;
  • lines 14–18: An appointment that has already been canceled (by double-clicking or by another administrator) triggers an error message, not an error page;
  • lines 22–25: deletion, followed by schema PRG.

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // who is logged in, and what are they allowed to do on this page?
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    private async Task<Rights> RightsAsync(ConnectedUser user)
    {
        if (user.Role != Role.USER)
        {
            return new Rights(Manager: true, Patient: null, PatientCanBook: false);
        }
        var patient = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        var upcoming = await application.GetClientUpcomingAppointmentsAsync(patient.Id);
        return new Rights(Manager: false, patient, PatientCanBook: upcoming.Count == 0);
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- utility functions

    // the hidden doctorId / day fields, common to the two POST forms
    private static bool ReadScheduleRequest(string? rawDoctorId, string? rawDay, out int doctorId, out DateOnly day)
    {
        doctorId = Input.PositiveInteger(rawDoctorId) ?? 0;
        return WebDates.IsValidDate(rawDay, out day) && doctorId > 0;
    }

    private static string ScheduleUrl(int doctorId, DateOnly day, int? book = null)
    {
        var url = $"/schedule?doctorId={doctorId}&day={WebDates.Iso(day)}";
        return book is null ? url : $"{url}&book={book}";
    }

    private static OptionView Option(Person p, bool selected) => new(p.Id, Labels.Label(p), selected);
}
  • lines 4–12: An administrator has full permissions; a patient can make a reservation if they have no upcoming appointments. The named arguments ([Manager: true]) make the call to the [record] constructor readable;
  • lines 18–21: reading the two hidden fields common to the POST forms. The [out] parameters are additional results from the method: it returns a Boolean (are the fields valid?) and, via its [out] parameters, the converted values. This is the process of [int.TryParse];
  • lines 24–27: the URL for a doctor’s schedule on a given day, possibly with the booking window open. All controller redirects generate this via this function: the URL for the page are written in a single location;
  • line 30: a drop-down list option (ID, label, selection), for both a doctor and a client: the parameter is of type [Person], the parent class of both entities.

docs.title: 11.16.3. Controllers/PersonsControllerBase.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/PersonsControllerBase.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The management of the doctors and that of the clients (reserved for the ADMIN) are
// IDENTICAL: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
// writing the same actions twice, we write them once in this
// ABSTRACT and GENERIC class, from which DoctorsController
// ([Route("doctors")]) and ClientsController ([Route("clients")]) inherit. Each
// subclass only has to provide its "configuration": which methods
// to call, which labels to display.
//
// The routes placed HERE ([HttpGet("add")]...) are inherited, and
// complete the route of the subclass. We therefore get, for each one:
//
//   GET  /doctors                    list
//   GET  /doctors/add                empty form
//   POST /doctors/add                creation
//   GET  /doctors/{id}/edit          pre-filled form
//   POST /doctors/{id}/edit          update
//   POST /doctors/{id}/delete        deletion
//
// (and the same URLs under /clients). The views are common too:
// Views/Persons/List.cshtml and Views/Persons/Form.cshtml.
//
// An abstract class is never taken for a controller by MVC: only
// its concrete subclasses are.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Business;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

// what each subclass must provide
public record PersonsConfig<T>(
    string Url, // "/doctors" or "/clients"
    PersonKeys Keys,
    Func<Task<List<T>>> List,
    Func<int, Task<T?>> Find,
    Func<PersonData, Task<T>> Add,
    Func<int, PersonData, Task<T>> Edit,
    Func<int, Task> Delete) where T : Person;

public abstract class PersonsControllerBase<T>(ApplicationModel application) : Controller where T : Person
{
    protected ApplicationModel Application { get; } = application;

    protected abstract PersonsConfig<T> Config { get; }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /doctors (or /clients)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> List()
    {
        var persons = await Config.List();
        return View("~/Views/Persons/List.cshtml", new PersonListModel
        {
            PageTitle = Config.Keys.Title,
            Keys = Config.Keys,
            AddUrl = $"{Config.Url}/add",
            Persons = persons
                .Select(p => new PersonView(p.Title, p.FirstName, p.LastName, p.User?.Login ?? "",
                    $"{Config.Url}/{p.Id}/edit", $"{Config.Url}/{p.Id}/delete"))
                .ToList(),
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /doctors/add
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("add")]
    public IActionResult AddForm() => ShowForm(null, new PersonValues());

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /doctors/add
    // [form] has been filled AND validated by MVC: ModelState says whether the
    // input is correct.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("add")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Add(PersonForm form)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return ShowForm(null, EnteredValues(form), Validation.ErrorsOf(ModelState));
        }
        try
        {
            var person = await Config.Add(Data(form));
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, Config.Keys.Added, MessageParams(person));
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        catch (BusinessException e)
        {
            return ShowBusinessError(null, EnteredValues(form), e);
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /doctors/{id}/edit
    // {id:int}: a "route constraint" - /doctors/abc/edit does not
    // match any route (404 page)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("{id:int}/edit")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> EditForm(int id)
    {
        var person = await Config.Find(id);
        if (person is null)
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        return ShowForm(id, new PersonValues
        {
            Title = person.Title,
            FirstName = person.FirstName,
            LastName = person.LastName,
            Login = person.User?.Login ?? "",
            Version = person.Version,
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /doctors/{id}/edit
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/edit")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Edit(int id, PersonForm form)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return ShowForm(id, EnteredValues(form), Validation.ErrorsOf(ModelState));
        }
        try
        {
            var person = await Config.Edit(id, Data(form));
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, Config.Keys.Edited, MessageParams(person));
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        catch (BusinessException e)
        {
            return ShowBusinessError(id, EnteredValues(form), e);
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /doctors/{id}/delete
    // (the "Are you sure?" confirmation is asked by the browser before
    // sending the form, see wwwroot/js/app.js)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/delete")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Delete(int id)
    {
        var person = await Config.Find(id);
        try
        {
            await Config.Delete(id);
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, Config.Keys.Deleted, MessageParams(person));
        }
        catch (BusinessException e)
        {
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, e.Key, new Dictionary<string, string>(e.Params));
        }
        return Redirect(Config.Url);
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

    // null id: creation form; otherwise: edit form
    private ViewResult ShowForm(
        int? id,
        PersonValues values,
        Dictionary<string, string>? errors = null,
        string? error = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? otherFields = null)
    {
        var creating = id is null;
        return View("~/Views/Persons/Form.cshtml", Validation.Prepare(
            new PersonFormModel
            {
                PageTitle = creating ? Config.Keys.Add : Config.Keys.Edit,
                Creating = creating,
                Action = creating ? $"{Config.Url}/add" : $"{Config.Url}/{id}/edit",
                ListUrl = Config.Url,
                Values = values,
            },
            errors, error, otherFields));
    }

    // a business rule refused the write: we redisplay the form,
    // with the user's input and the message of the business layer
    private IActionResult ShowBusinessError(int? id, PersonValues values, BusinessException e)
    {
        if (e.Key is "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND" or "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND")
        {
            // deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: back to the list
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, e.Key);
            return Redirect(Config.Url);
        }
        // the message goes at the bottom of the page; the fields concerned, if any, are
        // outlined in red so that the user immediately sees what to correct
        return ShowForm(id, values, null, e.Key, Validation.BusinessErrorFields.GetValueOrDefault(e.Key));
    }

    // what the user typed (password excluded: we never send it back to the browser)
    private static PersonValues EnteredValues(PersonForm f) => new()
    {
        Title = f.Title ?? "",
        FirstName = f.FirstName ?? "",
        LastName = f.LastName ?? "",
        Login = f.Login ?? "",
        Version = f.Version,
    };

    // the validated form -> the data expected by the business layer
    private static PersonData Data(PersonForm f) => new()
    {
        Title = f.Title!,
        LastName = f.LastName!,
        FirstName = f.FirstName!,
        Login = f.Login,
        Password = f.Password,
        Version = f.Version,
    };

    // {name} and {login} of the "added / updated / deleted" messages
    private static Dictionary<string, string> MessageParams(Person? person) => person is null
        ? new() { ["name"] = "", ["login"] = "" }
        : new() { ["name"] = $"{person.FirstName} {person.LastName}", ["login"] = person.User?.Login ?? "" };
}

The management of doctors and clients is identical. Rather than writing two similar controllers, we write their actions once, in an abstract and generic parent class. Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 15–20: the routes for doctors; the same ones exist in [/clients];
  • lines 22–23: the views are also shared (folder [Views/Persons]);
  • lines 25–26: MVC accepts only concrete classes as controllers: only [DoctorsController] and [ClientsController] receive requests;
  • lines 38–45: the configuration provided by each subclass: the base URL, the texts (translation keys, grouped in [record] and [PersonKeys] from [Models/ViewModels.cs]), and the functions to be called for listing, searching, adding, modifying, and deleting. [Func<int, Task<T?>>] is the type of a function that takes a [int] and returns a [Task<T?>]: this is how methods are stored in properties, to be called later. [where T : Person] is a constraint on the generic type: [T] will be either [Doctor] or [Client], two classes derived from [Person]; the code can therefore use [p.FirstName] or [p.User], which are common to all people;
  • Line 47: the parent class, which is generic (see the [ViewPage<TModel>] class in Example 22) and abstract. It receives [ApplicationModel] via its main constructor and passes it to its subclasses via the protected property [Application] ([protected]: visible only to subclasses);
  • line 51: an abstract property: each subclass must define it;
  • lines 56–69: the list. The route attributes set on a parent class’s methods are inherited: combined with the subclass’s [[Route("doctors")]], they yield [GET /doctors]. For each person, the model contains the URL for their Edit and Delete buttons. [p.User?.Login ?? ""]: the login for the associated account, or an empty string if the person does not have an account;
  • line 60: the view is specified by its full path. If only its name were used, MVC would search for it in the controller’s folder ([Views/Doctors] or [Views/Clients], see Example 13), whereas it is shared by both;
  • lines 75–76: the empty form;
  • lines 83–98: the addition, in three steps, as in Example 28. The parameter [form] was populated and validated by MVC prior to the call (see Example 19): an invalid entry redisplays the form, showing the entered values and a message below each incorrect field; a valid entry is passed to the business layer, then the browser is redirected to the list, with a flash message (PRG); a rejection by the business layer (a homonym, a login already in use) re-displays the form;
  • Lines 107–121: the pre-filled modification form. The route constraint [:int] (see Example 02) only accepts an integer identifier: [/doctors/abc/edit] does not correspond to any route, resulting in a 404 page ([ParseIntPipe] derived from [NestJS] resulted in a 400 error). A nonexistent person also results in a 404. The version number, a hidden field in the form, will be used for the optimistic lock (see example 28);
  • lines 128–143: the update, following the same pattern as the insertion;
  • lines 152–165: deletion. The person is retrieved beforehand to display their name in the confirmation message. A rejection from the business layer (e.g., a doctor who has appointments) results in a flash error message on the list page;
  • lines 171–188: the form for creation ([id] is equivalent to [null]), as for modification: only the title and the submission address ([Action]) change. [Validation.Prepare] (folder [Web]) populates the template with field-specific error messages, the footer message, and the fields to be highlighted in red;
  • lines 193–203: a person who has since been deleted (by another administrator) is listed again; other business errors re-display the form, with the footer message and the affected fields highlighted in red ([Validation.BusinessErrorFields] associates each error code with its corresponding fields: [firstName] and [lastName] for a homonym). [is "A" or "B"] compares a value to several constants;
  • lines 207–213: the values to be redisplayed—never the password;
  • lines 217–224: the data transmitted to the business layer. The [!] fields pose no risk: validation has verified the presence of these fields;
  • lines 228–230: the [{name}] and [{login}] parameters in the success messages: the person’s first and last name, and their login.

// =========================================================================
// Controllers/DoctorsController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Management of the doctors (ADMIN role only). All the actions are
// inherited from PersonsControllerBase: all that is left here is to say WHAT
// to call and WHICH labels to display.
//
// [Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")] placed on the CLASS applies to all its
// actions, including the inherited ones.
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize(Roles = "ADMIN")]
[Route("doctors")]
public class DoctorsController(ApplicationModel application) : PersonsControllerBase<Doctor>(application)
{
    protected override PersonsConfig<Doctor> Config => new(
        Url: "/doctors",
        Keys: new PersonKeys(
            Title: "DOCTORS.TITLE",
            Add: "DOCTORS.ADD",
            Edit: "DOCTORS.EDIT",
            Empty: "DOCTORS.EMPTY",
            ConfirmDelete: "DOCTORS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
            Added: "DOCTORS.ADDED",
            Edited: "DOCTORS.UPDATED",
            Deleted: "DOCTORS.DELETED"),
        List: Application.GetAllDoctorsAsync,
        Find: Application.GetDoctorByIdAsync,
        Add: Application.AddDoctorAsync,
        Edit: Application.EditDoctorAsync,
        Delete: Application.DeleteDoctorAsync);
}
  • Lines 20–22: Reserved for ADMIN. The attribute set on the class applies to all its actions, including inherited ones. The controller inherits from [PersonsControllerBase<Doctor>]: the parent class’s type, [T], becomes [Doctor]. Its main constructor passes [application] to the parent class’s constructor. (In [TypeScript], an explicit constructor had to be written so that [NestJS] would know what to inject; there is no need for that here);
  • lines 24–34: the configuration. [override] redefines the parent class’s abstract property; [=>] turns it into a computed property, which creates the object each time it is read. The named arguments ([Url:], [Keys:]...) make the list readable;
  • lines 35–39: the functions to be called, which are methods of [ApplicationModel]. [Application.GetAllDoctorsAsync], written without parentheses, does not call the method: it refers to it, and the compiler converts it to a value of the expected type [Func].
