docs.title: 11.16.6. Controllers/RegistrationController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/RegistrationController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// "Create a patient account": a patient who does not have an account yet
// creates it themselves. NON-protected routes (we do not have an account yet, by
// definition):
//
//   POST /register/access     "Create a patient account" button of the
//                             authentication page: checks the captcha of
//                             THIS page, then opens the form
//   GET  /register            the form
//   POST /register            the creation, then back to the login page
//
// The flow is protected against robots by ONE captcha, the one of the
// authentication page:
//   1. the "Create a patient account" button sends the login form
//      to /register/access; if the captcha is copied correctly, the server
//      issues a pass (see Auth/RegistrationPassService.cs);
//   2. without a valid pass, /register sends back to the
//      authentication page - typing the URL directly is useless;
//   3. the pass is consumed at creation: one solved captcha
//      allows creating ONE account;
//   4. in addition, the number of accounts created per hour and per IP address is
//      limited (see Auth/AttemptLimiterService.cs).
//
// The account created is exactly the one the ADMIN would create from the
// "Patients" page (same method of the business layer: AddClientAsync), except
// that the patient CHOOSES their login and password (required,
// with confirmation).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Business;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Route("register")]
public class RegistrationController(
    ApplicationModel application,
    CaptchaService captchaService,
    AttemptLimiterService limiter,
    RegistrationPassService passes) : Controller
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /register/access   fields: captchaId, captcha (those of the
    // authentication page; login and password, also sent, are ignored)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("access")]
    public IActionResult Access([FromForm] string? captchaId, [FromForm] string? captcha)
    {
        var ip = AuthController.IpAddress(HttpContext);

        // too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to go further
        var minutes = limiter.RegistrationBlockMinutes(ip);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", new() { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
            return Redirect("/login");
        }

        // missing or wrong captcha: back to the authentication page, with
        // a new image (a failure counts as a login failure)
        if (!captchaService.Verify(captchaId, captcha))
        {
            limiter.LoginFailure(ip, "");
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT");
            return Redirect("/login");
        }

        // correct captcha: we issue the pass and open the form
        Response.Cookies.Append(RegistrationPassService.Cookie, passes.Issue(), RegistrationPassService.GetCookieOptions());
        return Redirect("/register");
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /register
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Form()
    {
        if (!HasPass())
        {
            return BackToLogin();
        }
        return Show(new PersonValues());
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /register
    // The [form] parameter is filled and VALIDATED by MVC before the call:
    // the result of the validation is in ModelState.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Create(RegistrationForm form)
    {
        if (!HasPass())
        {
            return BackToLogin();
        }
        var ip = AuthController.IpAddress(HttpContext);
        var values = new PersonValues
        {
            Title = form.Title ?? "Mr",
            FirstName = form.FirstName ?? "",
            LastName = form.LastName ?? "",
            Login = form.Login ?? "",
        };

        // 1. too many accounts created recently from this address?
        var minutes = limiter.RegistrationBlockMinutes(ip);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return Show(values, null, "ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", null, new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }

        // 2. all the input errors at once (fields + confirmation):
        //    the user corrects them all in one go
        var errors = Validation.ErrorsOf(ModelState);
        if (!errors.ContainsKey("password") && !errors.ContainsKey("confirmation") && form.Password != form.Confirmation)
        {
            errors["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER";
        }
        if (errors.Count > 0)
        {
            return Show(values, errors);
        }

        // 3. the creation (client + USER account, in a transaction)
        try
        {
            // "!": we assert to the compiler that these values are not null -
            // which is true, since the validation ([Required]) succeeded
            await application.AddClientAsync(new PersonData
            {
                Title = form.Title!,
                LastName = form.LastName!,
                FirstName = form.FirstName!,
                Login = form.Login,
                Password = form.Password,
            });
        }
        catch (BusinessException e)
        {
            // login or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
            return Show(values, null, e.Key, Validation.BusinessErrorFields.GetValueOrDefault(e.Key));
        }

        // 4. the pass has been used: it will not allow creating a 2nd account
        passes.Consume(Request.Cookies[RegistrationPassService.Cookie]);
        Response.Cookies.Delete(RegistrationPassService.Cookie, new CookieOptions { Path = "/register" });
        limiter.RegistrationSuccess(ip);

        // 5. back to the login page, login pre-filled
        Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, "REGISTRATION.DONE", new() { ["login"] = form.Login! });
        return Redirect($"/login?login={Uri.EscapeDataString(form.Login!)}");
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

    private bool HasPass() => passes.IsValid(Request.Cookies[RegistrationPassService.Cookie]);

    // no valid pass: back to the authentication page
    private RedirectResult BackToLogin()
    {
        Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT");
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

    // the form; never any password sent back to the browser
    private ViewResult Show(
        PersonValues values,
        Dictionary<string, string>? errors = null,
        string? error = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? otherFields = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? errorParams = null) =>
        View("Registration", Validation.Prepare(
            new RegistrationModel { PageTitle = "REGISTRATION.TITLE", Values = values },
            errors, error, otherFields, errorParams));
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 14–24: protection against bots, in four steps. The CAPTCHA and attempt limiter were introduced in Example 27;
  • lines 40–45: The controller does not have the [[Authorize]] attribute; its pages are open to everyone. It receives four services via injection;
  • lines 51–52: The “Create a patient account” button on the login page sends the login form to this address (attribute [formaction]; see Example 20). Only the CAPTCHA fields are read;
  • line 54: the browser’s address IP, via a static method from [AuthController];
  • lines 57–61: Too many accounts have been created from this address within the last hour: the user is redirected to the login page, with a pop-up message indicating the number of minutes to wait. [new() { ["minutes"] = ... }] creates the message parameter dictionary: its type is inferred from the parameter of [Flash.Put];
  • lines 66–70: a missing or incorrect CAPTCHA counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username): a bot cannot keep trying indefinitely. Returning to the login page displays a new image;
  • lines 74–75: the CAPTCHA is correct: a pass (see [Auth/RegistrationPassService.cs]) is stored in a cookie, and the browser is redirected to the form;
  • Lines 81–88: the form, only with a valid pass. Typing the address [/register] directly is pointless;
  • lines 96–97: creation. The form [RegistrationForm] (folder [Models]) was linked and validated by MVC;
  • lines 99–101: The pass is verified again: the request POST might have been sent without going through the form;
  • lines 104–109: the values to be redisplayed in case of an error, without the password. The default title is [Mr];
  • lines 113–116: the time limit, checked again at the time of creation;
  • lines 121–128: input errors, field by field (see Example 19). The match between the password and its confirmation—which spans two fields—is verified here manually; it is tested only if these two fields are otherwise correct. All errors are reported together: the user corrects them all at once;
  • lines 136–148: creation of the customer and their account USER, using the business layer method employed by ADMIN. If a username or first-name-last-name combination is already taken, the form is re-displayed with the relevant fields highlighted in red; the pass remains valid;
  • Lines 152–154: The pass has been used: it is consumed on the server side, and its cookie is deleted. To delete a cookie, you must specify the same path ([Path]) as when it was created: the pass cookie is sent only to addresses [/register...]. The creation is finally counted toward the hourly limit;
  • lines 157–158: return to the login page, with the username pre-filled, and a success message. [Uri.EscapeDataString] encodes the username so it can be included in a URL;
  • line 163: the pass is read from the request cookie;
  • lines 166–169: if no pass is present, return to the login page with a message;
  • lines 173–181: the form, prepared by [Validation.Prepare], is the same as those for doctors and clients. [errorParams] is used for the parameters of the footer message (the number of minutes).

docs.title: 11.16.7. Controllers/PatientAreaController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/PatientAreaController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The PERSONAL pages of the patient (USER role), the one they see right
// after logging in:
//
//   GET  /my-area                  home page: [Manage my account],
//                                  [View a schedule], and their upcoming appointment
//   POST /my-area/cancel           cancels THEIR appointment
//   GET  /my-account               form to edit their account
//   POST /my-account               update
//   POST /my-account/delete        deletion of the account (and of its appointments)
//
// Golden rule of this controller: the patient concerned is ALWAYS the one of the
// token (Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync), never an identifier sent by the
// browser. A patient can therefore neither see, nor modify, nor cancel what
// belongs to another patient, even by forging their requests themselves.
//
// Any modification or deletion of the account requires the CURRENT
// password: someone who found a session left open could
// neither change the password, nor delete the account. The current password
// errors are counted as login failures (same limit).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Auth;
using RdvMedecins.Entities;
using RdvMedecins.Business;
using RdvMedecins.Models;
using RdvMedecins.Web;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

[Authorize(Roles = "USER")]
public class PatientAreaController(
    ApplicationModel application,
    AuthService authService,
    AttemptLimiterService limiter) : Controller
{
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /my-area
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("my-area")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Area()
    {
        var patient = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        var appointments = await application.GetClientUpcomingAppointmentsAsync(patient.Id);
        return View("Area", new AreaModel
        {
            PageTitle = "AREA.TITLE",
            Patient = Labels.Label(patient),
            Appointments = appointments.Select(a => new AppointmentView(
                a.Id,
                WebDates.FormatDay(a.Day),
                WebDates.Time(a.Slot),
                Labels.Label(a.Slot.Doctor),
                // link to the doctor's schedule on that day: the patient sees their name there
                $"/schedule?doctorId={a.Slot.Doctor.Id}&day={WebDates.Iso(a.Day)}")).ToList(),
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /my-area/cancel   field: appointmentId
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("my-area/cancel")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> CancelAppointment([FromForm] string? appointmentId)
    {
        var patient = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        var appointment = Input.PositiveInteger(appointmentId) is int id ? await application.GetAppointmentByIdAsync(id) : null;
        // an appointment that does not exist, and the one of ANOTHER patient, get
        // the same answer: we reveal nothing about the appointments of the others
        if (appointment is null || appointment.ClientId != patient.Id)
        {
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND");
        }
        else
        {
            await application.DeleteAppointmentAsync(appointment);
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, "SCHEDULE.CANCELLED");
        }
        return Redirect("/my-area");
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // GET /my-account
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpGet("my-account")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> AccountForm()
    {
        var patient = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        return Show(new PersonValues
        {
            Title = patient.Title,
            FirstName = patient.FirstName,
            LastName = patient.LastName,
            Login = patient.User.Login,
            Version = patient.Version,
        });
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /my-account
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("my-account")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> EditAccount(MyAccountForm form)
    {
        var patient = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        var values = new PersonValues
        {
            Title = form.Title ?? patient.Title,
            FirstName = form.FirstName ?? "",
            LastName = form.LastName ?? "",
            Login = form.Login ?? "",
            Version = form.Version,
        };

        var errors = Validation.ErrorsOf(ModelState);
        if (!errors.ContainsKey("password") && form.Password is not null && form.Password != form.Confirmation)
        {
            errors["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER";
        }
        if (errors.Count > 0)
        {
            return Show(values, errors);
        }

        // the current password
        var passwordError = await CheckCurrentPasswordAsync(patient, form.CurrentPassword);
        if (passwordError is not null)
        {
            var (key, messageParams) = passwordError.Value;
            return Show(
                values,
                key == "ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD" ? new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { ["currentPassword"] = key } : null,
                key,
                null,
                messageParams);
        }

        try
        {
            var client = await application.EditClientAsync(patient.Id, new PersonData
            {
                Title = form.Title!,
                LastName = form.LastName!,
                FirstName = form.FirstName!,
                Login = form.Login,
                Password = form.Password, // null = unchanged
                Version = form.Version,
            });
            // the login and the display name are IN the token: we issue a
            // new one, otherwise the navigation bar would keep the old name
            authService.SetToken(Response, client.User);
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, "MY_ACCOUNT.UPDATED");
            return Redirect("/my-area");
        }
        catch (BusinessException e)
        {
            return Show(values, null, e.Key, Validation.BusinessErrorFields.GetValueOrDefault(e.Key));
        }
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // POST /my-account/delete   field: deletePassword
    // The account, the client and ALL their appointments disappear together,
    // then the patient is logged out.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    [HttpPost("my-account/delete")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> DeleteAccount([FromForm] string? deletePassword)
    {
        var patient = await Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync(application, User);
        var passwordError = await CheckCurrentPasswordAsync(patient, deletePassword);
        if (passwordError is not null)
        {
            var (key, messageParams) = passwordError.Value;
            Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Danger, key, messageParams);
            return Redirect("/my-account");
        }
        await application.DeleteClientAsync(patient.Id);
        AuthService.ClearToken(Response);
        Flash.Put(HttpContext, FlashType.Success, "MY_ACCOUNT.DELETED");
        return Redirect("/login");
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------------- private methods

    // null if the current password is correct; otherwise the key of the message
    // (and its parameters). The return type is a nullable "tuple".
    private async Task<(string Key, Dictionary<string, string>? Params)?> CheckCurrentPasswordAsync(
        Client patient, string? password)
    {
        var ip = AuthController.IpAddress(HttpContext);
        var login = patient.User.Login;
        var minutes = limiter.LoginBlockMinutes(ip, login);
        if (minutes > 0)
        {
            return ("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["minutes"] = minutes.ToString() });
        }
        var ok = !string.IsNullOrEmpty(password) && await authService.ValidateUserAsync(login, password) is not null;
        if (!ok)
        {
            limiter.LoginFailure(ip, login);
            return ("ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD", null);
        }
        return null;
    }

    private ViewResult Show(
        PersonValues values,
        Dictionary<string, string>? errors = null,
        string? error = null,
        IEnumerable<string>? otherFields = null,
        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? errorParams = null) =>
        View("Account", Validation.Prepare(
            new MyAccountModel { PageTitle = "MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE", Values = values },
            errors, error, otherFields, errorParams));
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 14–17: the golden rule of this controller: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token, never an identifier sent by the browser;
  • lines 35–39: reserved for patients. The controller has no [[Route]] attribute: each action provides its full address, since they do not share a prefix ([/my-area], [/my-account]);
  • lines 44–59: the “My area” page. [Patient.ConnectedPatientAsync] identifies the user based on the token; if their account has been deleted since they logged in, it triggers a [InvalidSessionException], which the [Web/HtmlExceptionFilter.cs] filter redirects back to the login page. The date is formatted by [WebDates.FormatDay] according to the language of the request, set by the localization middleware (see Example 22); each appointment includes a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day;
  • lines 66–82: cancellation of the patient’s appointment. [condition ? value1 : value2] returns the appointment here, or [null] if the ID is invalid. A nonexistent appointment and one belonging to another patient (line 73) receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments;
  • lines 88–98: the account form, pre-filled, with the version number (optimistic lock);
  • lines 105–106: the modification process, in three steps: validation, verification of the current password, business logic;
  • lines 109–115: the values to be redisplayed in case of an error, never passwords;
  • lines 118–125: input errors. The new password is optional (blank: unchanged); its confirmation is compared only if it was entered;
  • lines 129–138: the current password. [var (key, messageParams) = ...] parses the pair returned by the verification. An incorrect password is displayed below its field and at the bottom of the page; a lockout (too many attempts) is shown only at the bottom of the page, along with the number of minutes;
  • lines 143–150: modification by the business layer, which applies the same rules as for ADMIN (uniqueness, optimistic lock);
  • line 154: the token contains the login and the display name: after a change, a new token is issued; otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name;
  • lines 158–160: a rejection by the business layer re-displays the form, with the relevant fields highlighted in red;
  • lines 169–183: Deleting the account, which also requires the current password. An error is indicated by a pop-up message on the account page (PRG);
  • lines 180–181: Deletion of the record, the account, and all appointments (the business layer method used by ADMIN), followed by logout: the token cookie is cleared;
  • lines 190–191: verification of the current password. This returns [null] if the password is correct; otherwise, it returns a tuple: a pair of named values (the message key and its parameters). The final [?] makes this tuple “nullable”;
  • lines 195–198: The current password is subject to the same limiter as the connection (see Example 27). Someone who found a session that remained open would be unable to change the password, delete the account, or attempt passwords indefinitely;
  • lines 200–204: the authentication process itself, handled by [AuthService]; a failed authentication attempt is counted as a failed login attempt;
  • lines 209–217: the account form.

docs.title: 11.16.8. Controllers/ErrorController.cs
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// Controllers/ErrorController.cs
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The error page (400, 403, 404, 500).
//
// It is never reached through a link: it is the middlewares
// UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/error/{0}") and
// UseExceptionHandler("/error/500") (see Program.cs) that RE-EXECUTE the
// failed request with this address, to build the page to send back
// instead of an empty response or an exception.
//
// [Route] without [HttpGet]: the action accepts all HTTP methods - the
// re-executed request keeps its original method (a refused POST stays a POST).
// =========================================================================

using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using RdvMedecins.Models;

namespace RdvMedecins.Controllers;

public class ErrorController : Controller
{
    private static readonly Dictionary<int, string> Messages = new()
    {
        [StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest] = "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST",
        [StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden] = "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN",
        [StatusCodes.Status404NotFound] = "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND",
    };

    [Route("error/{code:int}")]
    public IActionResult Show(int code)
    {
        // the page keeps the original error code (404 stays 404...); an
        // unexpected code becomes a 500 error
        if (code < 400 || code > 599)
        {
            code = StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError;
        }
        Response.StatusCode = code;
        return View("Error", new ErrorModel
        {
            PageTitle = "ERROR_PAGE.TITLE",
            Code = code,
            Message = Messages.GetValueOrDefault(code, "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR"),
        });
    }
}

This is the controller from Example 24, with translated messages:

  • lines 23–28: the message key for each error code. [static readonly]: a single dictionary, created when the class is loaded and never replaced;
  • lines 30–31: [[Route]], which lacks the HTTP method, accepts all methods: a re-executed POST request (for example, a patient attempting a cancellation reserved for administrators) remains a POST request;
  • lines 35–37: a non-error code HTTP (a manually entered [/error/200] address) becomes a 500 error;
  • line 39: the page retains the original error code;
  • lines 40–44: the page template. [GetValueOrDefault] returns the key associated with the code, or [ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR] for any other code (500 in particular).

docs.title: 11.17. The Views
docs.text:
The views have almost nothing to decide: their template has been prepared by the controllers in the classes of the [Models/ViewModels.cs] file (which buttons to display, which URL elements, which translation keys). Each view declares the type of its template ([@model], see Example 13): a typo in [@Model.Xxx] will cause a compilation error. Each view also begins with a comment [Razor] [@* ... *@] that describes its role; these comments do not appear in the pages sent to the browser.

One difference from the examples in Chapter 4: the case study does not use Tag Helpers. Partial views are inserted using [@await Html.PartialAsync("_Name")], the equivalent of the [<partial name="_Name">] tag from Example 15. A second, optional argument provides the partial view’s model; without it, the partial view receives the page’s model. The method is asynchronous (the partial view may need to be compiled or read from disk): [await] waits for its result.

@* =========================================================================
   Views/_ViewImports.cshtml
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Read before EACH view of this folder and its subfolders: the common
   "using"s, and the parent class of all the views (Web/ViewPage.cs), which
   brings them @T("KEY"), CurrentUser, FlashMessage...
   TModel designates the type of the model of each view (@model ...).
   ========================================================================= *@
@using RdvMedecins
@using RdvMedecins.Models
@using RdvMedecins.Web
@inherits RdvMedecins.Web.ViewPage<TModel>
  • lines 9–11: the namespaces whose types are used by the views: the view templates ([RdvMedecins.Models]), the flash messages ([RdvMedecins.Web]);
  • line 12: the parent class of all views, [Web/ViewPage.cs], as in Example 22. It provides them with the translation [@T("KEY")], the language [Language], the logged-in user [CurrentUser], the flash message [FlashMessage], the requested path [CurrentPath], and the method [Active] (active menu item in the navigation bar). In version [NestJS], this information was passed through [res.locals]. There is no [@addTagHelper] directive: the application does not use Tag Helpers.

@* =========================================================================
   Views/_ViewStart.cshtml
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Executed before each view: all the pages use the common layout
   Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml (hbs did it automatically for
   views/layout.hbs; here, we say it explicitly).
   ========================================================================= *@
@{
    Layout = "_Layout";
}
  • Line 9: All pages use the [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml] template (see Example 15). [Handlebars] automatically used [views/layout.hbs]; [Razor] requires this to be specified.

docs.title: 11.17.1.3. Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   The layout COMMON to all the pages. The page requested by the controller
   (Schedule.cshtml, Login.cshtml...) is inserted at the location
   @RenderBody().

   Razor ESCAPES everything it displays with @ (the characters < > & " '
   become < >...): protection against HTML injection through a
   typed name, for example. To insert HTML as is, it must be requested
   explicitly (@Html.Raw, see _Captcha.cshtml).

   Messages: a success is displayed at the TOP of the page (_Flash), an error at the
   BOTTOM, on a light pink background (_Errors).

   The layout shares the model of the page: if it is a ViewModel (see
   Models/ViewModels.cs), we read the title and the error of the page from it.
   ========================================================================= *@
@{
    var page = ViewData.Model as ViewModel;
}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="@Language">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>@T(page?.PageTitle ?? "APP.TITLE") - @T("APP.TITLE")</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    @await Html.PartialAsync("_Navbar")
    @await Html.PartialAsync("_Flash")
    @RenderBody()
    @await Html.PartialAsync("_Errors")
  </div>
  @* the "Are you sure?" dialog, hidden as long as it is not needed *@
  @await Html.PartialAsync("_Confirmation")
  <script src="/js/app.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • Line 20: The template shares the page model, accessible via [ViewData.Model] (of type [object]). All page templates derive from the abstract class [ViewModel], which contains the title key ([PageTitle]) and the page error ([Error]). [as ViewModel] returns [null] if the template is not a [ViewModel]: the template works with any page;
  • line 23: the page's language (see example 22);
  • Line 27: the title, translated, for example, “Schedule - RdvMedecins.” Unlike Example 22, the key is not set by the view in [ViewData]: it is provided by the controller in the typed model. [page?.PageTitle] is equal to [null] if [page] is [null], and the operator [??] then replaces the key with [APP.TITLE];
  • lines 28–29: the style sheets, served by [UseStaticFiles] from the [wwwroot] folder: [Bootstrap] ([wwwroot/lib/bootstrap]) and the application-specific style sheet;
  • lines 33–36: the navigation bar, the success message (at the top), the requested page ([@RenderBody()]), and the error area (at the bottom);
  • lines 39–40: the confirmation window (hidden) and its script (see Example 21), loaded at the bottom of the page.

docs.title: 11.17.1.4. Views/Shared/_Navbar.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Shared/_Navbar.cshtml - the navigation bar.

   Title, FR/EN, role, name, logout - and a menu whose entries
   depend on the role: "Doctors" and "Patients" appear only for
   the ADMIN. It is only a display convenience: the real protection is
   the [Authorize(Roles = ...)] of the controllers (a USER who types /doctors
   by hand gets a 403 page). A patient (USER) also has their
   "My area" menu.
   ========================================================================= *@
@{
    var user = CurrentUser;
}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">@T("APP.TITLE")</span>

  @if (user is not null)
  {
    <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
      @if (user.IsPatient)
      {
        <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link @Active("/my-")" href="/my-area">@T("APP.MENU_MY_AREA")</a></li>
      }
      <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link @Active("/schedule")" href="/schedule">@T("APP.MENU_SCHEDULE")</a></li>
      @if (user.IsAdmin)
      {
        <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link @Active("/doctors")" href="/doctors">@T("APP.MENU_DOCTORS")</a></li>
        <li class="nav-item"><a class="nav-link @Active("/clients")" href="/clients">@T("APP.MENU_PATIENTS")</a></li>
      }
    </ul>
  }
  else
  {
    <div class="me-auto"></div>
  }

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    @* FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), the active language highlighted *@
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      <a class="btn @(Language == "fr" ? "btn-light" : "btn-outline-light")" href="/language/fr">FR</a>
      <a class="btn @(Language == "en" ? "btn-light" : "btn-outline-light")" href="/language/en">EN</a>
    </div>

    @if (user is not null)
    {
      <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">@user.Role</span>
      <span class="text-white">@user.Name</span>
      @* logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button *@
      <form method="post" action="/logout" class="m-0">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">@T("APP.LOGOUT")</button>
      </form>
    }
  </div>
</nav>
  • line 12: the logged-in user, as described by the [ViewUser] class of [Web/ViewPage.cs] (login, name, role, [IsAdmin], [IsPatient]), derived from the token JWT. It is set to [null] on public pages (login, account creation);
  • lines 17–31: The menus depend on the role: “My area” for a patient, “Doctors” and “Patients” for the ADMIN. This is merely for convenience: security is ensured by the [[Authorize(Roles = ...)]] attributes of the controllers (a patient who manually enters [/doctors] will receive a 403 page). [Active("/doctors")] returns [active] if the requested path begins with [/doctors]: [Bootstrap] then highlights this menu. The prefix [/my-] covers both patient pages, [/my-area] and [/my-account];
  • line 34: without menus, an empty block takes its place ([me-auto]: automatic right margin), so that the rest of the content remains to the right of the bar;
  • lines 40–41: the links FR / EN from Example 22. The expression [@( ... )] is enclosed in parentheses because it contains spaces (see Example 14);
  • lines 44–52: the role, name, and logout button in a POST form (see Example 21).

docs.title: 11.17.1.5. Views/Shared/_Flash.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Shared/_Flash.cshtml - the SUCCESS message put by the previous
   action (appointment saved, doctor added...), displayed only
   once, at the top of the page (see Web/Flash.cs).
   An ERROR flash message, for its part, is displayed at the bottom of the page, by
   _Errors.cshtml.
   ========================================================================= *@
@{
    var flash = FlashMessage;
}
@if (flash is { Type: FlashType.Success })
{
  <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">
    @T(flash.Key, flash.Params)
  </div>
}
  • line 9: the flash message posted by the previous action (see example 20 and [Web/Flash.cs]). Reading a flash message clears it; since the page reads it twice (here and in [_Errors.cshtml]), the [Flash] class stores it, once read, in [HttpContext.Items] (see Chapter 6);
  • line 11: [flash is { Type: FlashType.Success }] is a property pattern: the condition is true if [flash] is not [null] and if its property [Type] is equal to [FlashType.Success]. Only a success message is displayed here;
  • line 14: the message is a key; its possible parameters ([name], [login], [minutes]) are a dictionary, passed to the second form of the [T] method. [role="status"]: A screen reader announces the message without interrupting the user.

docs.title: 11.17.1.6. Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml - the error zone, at the BOTTOM of each page,
   on a light pink background (.error-zone class, see wwwroot/css/styles.css).

   It gathers the two possible sources of error:
     - Error: the error of the displayed page (refused form, login or
       first + last name already used, invalid date, incorrect password...);
     - an error flash message, put by the previous action before a
       redirection (slot already booked, deletion refused...).

   role="alert": a screen reader announces the message as soon as the
   page is displayed, even if it is at the bottom.
   ========================================================================= *@
@{
    var page = ViewData.Model as ViewModel;
    var error = page?.Error;
    var flash = FlashMessage;
    var flashError = flash is { Type: FlashType.Danger } ? flash : null;
}
@if (error is not null || flashError is not null)
{
  <div class="error-zone" role="alert">
    @if (error is not null)
    {
      <div>@T(error, page!.ErrorParams)</div>
    }
    @if (flashError is not null)
    {
      <div>@T(flashError.Key, flashError.Params)</div>
    }
  </div>
}
  • Lines 15–18: the two sources of error: the error on the displayed page (property [Error] of the template: form rejected, incorrect password, etc.), and a flash error message displayed before a redirect (slot already reserved, deletion rejected, etc.);
  • Lines 20–22: The field is displayed if either one is present. [role="alert"]: A screen reader announces the message as soon as the page is displayed, even though it is at the bottom. The class [error-zone] is defined in [wwwroot/css/styles.css];
  • line 25: the operator [!] tells the compiler that [page] is not [null]: it cannot deduce this on its own, even though it is certain because [error], read from [page], is not.

docs.title: 11.17.1.7. Views/Shared/_Confirmation.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Shared/_Confirmation.cshtml - the "Are you sure?" modal dialog.

   It replaces the window.confirm() box of the browser, which can neither be
   styled, nor translated (its buttons stay in the language of the
   browser, not in that of the page).

   A SINGLE dialog for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first. Its
   labels are translated here, by the server, like the rest of the page;
   the small wwwroot/js/app.js script merely displays it, puts in it
   the message specific to the form (data-confirmation attribute), and sends
   the form if the user confirms.

   Same Bootstrap classes as the booking dialog (Schedule/_Booking.cshtml).
   ========================================================================= *@
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="confirmation-modal-title" aria-describedby="confirmation-modal-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="confirmation-modal-title">@T("CONFIRMATION.TITLE")</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="no" aria-label="@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA")"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          @* "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes
             "Cancel this appointment?", and a "Cancel" button would be ambiguous there *@
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">@T("CONFIRMATION.NO")</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">@T("CONFIRMATION.YES")</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The window from Example 21, with labels translated by the server—like the rest of the page—and accessibility attributes:

  • line 16: a single window for the entire page, initially hidden ([d-none]);
  • lines 18–19: [role="alertdialog"] indicates a window waiting for a response; [aria-modal="true"] indicates that the rest of the page is inactive; [aria-labelledby] and [aria-describedby] designate the title and the message read by a screen reader;
  • line 24: the close button, which means “No” ([data-action="no"]). It has no text: [aria-label] provides a name for screen readers;
  • Lines 32–33: “No, go back” rather than “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context.

docs.title: 11.17.1.8. Views/Auth/_Captcha.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Auth/_Captcha.cshtml - the captcha of the authentication page
   (see Auth/CaptchaService.cs). It protects both the login and
   the access to account creation ("Create a patient account" button).

   @Html.Raw(...): the SVG image is inserted AS IS in the page, without
   escaping. It is harmless here because this SVG is built by the
   server itself and contains nothing that comes from the user - we would
   NEVER do this with user input.

   The hidden captchaId field tells the server WHICH captcha to check; the right
   answer, for its part, is never sent to the browser.
   "Another image" simply reloads the page (path = the current URL).
   ========================================================================= *@
@model RdvMedecins.Auth.Captcha
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">@T("CAPTCHA.LABEL")</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="@T("CAPTCHA.IMAGE_ALT")">@Html.Raw(Model.Svg)</div>
    <a class="small" href="@CurrentPath">@T("CAPTCHA.NEW_IMAGE")</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captchaId" value="@Model.Id">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off" spellcheck="false" required
         class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">@T("CAPTCHA.HELP")</div>
</div>
  • line 15: the partial view has its own template, the CAPTCHA generated by [Auth/CaptchaService.cs] (see example 27): its ID and image;
  • line 19: the image SVG is inserted as-is (see example 14): it is generated by the server, with no input from the user. [role="img"] and [aria-label] generate an image for screen readers;
  • Line 20: “Another image” simply reloads the current page: a new CAPTCHA is generated;
  • line 22: the captcha ID, in a hidden field: it tells the server which captcha to verify. The correct answer, however, never leaves the server;
  • lines 23–24: the input. [autocomplete="off"], [autocapitalize="off"], and [spellcheck="false"] prevent the browser from suggesting, capitalizing, or correcting the copied characters.

docs.title: 11.17.1.9. Views/Shared/_PersonFields.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Shared/_PersonFields.cshtml - the identity fields (title,
   first name, last name), common to three forms: the ADMIN's doctor/client form,
   "Create a patient account" and "Manage my account".
   The partial receives the model of the page that inserts it (a FormView):
   values, message under each field, fields outlined in red.

   selected="@selected": a boolean attribute. Razor writes selected="selected"
   if the value is true, and OMITS the attribute if it is false.
   ========================================================================= *@
@model FormView
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="title">@T("PERSONS.TITLE_LABEL")</label>
  <select id="title" name="title" class="form-select @Model.InvalidClass("title")">
    @foreach (var (value, selected) in Model.Titles)
    {
      <option value="@value" selected="@selected">@value</option>
    }
  </select>
  @if (Model.ErrorOf("title") is { } titleError)
  {
    <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(titleError)</div>
  }
</div>

<div class="row g-3 mb-3">
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="firstName">@T("PERSONS.FIRSTNAME_LABEL")</label>
    <input id="firstName" name="firstName" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("firstName")" value="@Model.Values.FirstName">
    @if (Model.ErrorOf("firstName") is { } firstNameError)
    {
      <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(firstNameError)</div>
    }
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="lastName">@T("PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL")</label>
    <input id="lastName" name="lastName" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("lastName")" value="@Model.Values.LastName">
    @if (Model.ErrorOf("lastName") is { } lastNameError)
    {
      <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(lastNameError)</div>
    }
  </div>
</div>

The identity fields (title, first name, last name), common to three forms: doctor or client of ADMIN, account creation, and patient account management.

  • Line 11: [FormView] is the parent (abstract) class for the templates of these three forms. It contains the entered values ([Values]), the error message for each rejected field ([Errors]), and the fields to be highlighted in red ([InvalidFields]). The partial view therefore accepts the template for each of the three pages;
  • lines 14–19: the list of titles. [Model.Titles] returns tuples (value, selected?); [var (value, selected)] breaks down each tuple into two variables. [selected="@selected"] is a Boolean attribute, written only if the value is true (see Example 17). [InvalidClass("title")] returns [is-invalid] if the field is to be framed in red (see Example 19);
  • lines 20–23: the field’s error message, if any. [ErrorOf] returns the message, or [null]; the condition [is { } titleError] is true if the value is not [null], and then stores it in the new variable [titleError];
  • Lines 26–45: the first name and last name, following the same format, side by side on a sufficiently wide screen (grid [Bootstrap]: [col-sm-6]). The attributes [maxlength] and [required] are merely for convenience: forms that insert this partial view have the attribute [novalidate], and the server handles validation.

docs.title: 11.17.1.10. Views/Schedule/_Booking.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Schedule/_Booking.cshtml - the booking dialog.

   Same technique as the Angular client (booking-dialog): the REAL Bootstrap
   classes of a modal dialog (.modal, .modal-backdrop...), made
   visible "hard-coded" (show d-block) rather than by the JavaScript of
   Bootstrap. The difference: it is the SERVER that decides to display it
   (&book=... parameter of the URL), and closing it amounts to following a link
   to the same page without this parameter.
   ========================================================================= *@
@model ScheduleModel
@{
    var booking = Model.Booking!;
}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="booking-title">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="/schedule/book" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="booking-title">@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE")</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="@Model.BackUrl" aria-label="@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA")"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT", ("time", booking.Time))</p>

        @* what the server needs to know in addition to the chosen patient *@
        <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="@Model.DoctorId">
        <input type="hidden" name="day" value="@Model.Day">
        <input type="hidden" name="slotId" value="@booking.SlotId">

        @if (booking.Patient is not null)
        {
          @* a patient books for themselves: no list to choose from
             (and the server ignores any clientId anyway) *@
          <p class="mb-0">@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL"): <strong>@booking.Patient</strong></p>
        }
        else
        {
          <label class="form-label" for="clientId">@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL")</label>
          <select id="clientId" name="clientId" class="form-select" required autofocus>
            <option value="">@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT")</option>
            @foreach (var client in booking.Clients)
            {
              <option value="@client.Id">@client.Label</option>
            }
          </select>
        }
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="@Model.BackUrl">@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL")</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">@T("BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM")</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>
  • Line 11: The partial view receives the calendar page template. [Model.Booking!]: the page inserts it only if [Booking] is not [null], which the operator [!] asserts to the compiler;
  • lines 15–16: the classes [Bootstrap] for a modal window and its gray background, made visible “hard-coded” ([show d-block]): the server decides to display the window when URL contains the parameter [book]. The [JavaScript] from [Bootstrap] is not used (it isn’t even loaded);
  • line 18: the window’s content is the reservation form itself;
  • line 21: closing the window follows a link to the same calendar, without the [book] parameter ([BackUrl], prepared by the controller);
  • line 25: “Slot 8:00 - 8:20”: a translation parameter;
  • lines 28–30: hidden fields: additional information the server needs in addition to the selected patient;
  • lines 32–48: a patient sees their name; an administrator (ADMIN, DOCTOR) selects the patient from a list. The first option has an empty value: with [required], the browser requires that a real patient be selected. [autofocus] places the cursor in the list;
  • lines 52–53: “Cancel” is a link, as is the X; “Confirm” submits the form.

docs.title: 11.17.2.1. Views/Auth/Login.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Auth/Login.cshtml - the login form.
   An ordinary HTML <form>: the browser itself sends login,
   password and captcha answer with POST /login, without JavaScript. On
   failure, the server sends back THIS page, with the login already typed, a
   NEW captcha and the error, displayed at the bottom of the page by the layout.

   @model: the type of the view model. The compiler checks each
   @Model.Xxx (a typo is a compilation error).
   ========================================================================= *@
@model LoginModel
@{
    var loginTyped = Model.Login != "";
}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">@T("LOGIN.TITLE")</h5>

      <form method="post" action="/login">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">@T("LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="@Model.Login" required autofocus="@(!loginTyped)">
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">@T("LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required autofocus="@loginTyped">
        </div>

        @await Html.PartialAsync("_Captcha", Model.Captcha)

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">@T("LOGIN.SUBMIT")</button>

        @* no account yet: a patient can create one themselves.
           It is NOT a simple link: it is a second submit button of
           THIS form, which goes to another address (formaction). The
           server checks the captcha above there before opening the account
           creation page (see RegistrationController).
           formnovalidate: the browser does not require login and password
           (useless to create an account); it is the server that checks
           the captcha. Enter in a field always triggers the FIRST
           button of the form, "Log in". *@
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="/register/access" formnovalidate>@T("LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT")</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">@T("LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT_HELP")</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        @T("LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS")
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - @T("LOGIN.DEMO_ADMIN")</li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - @T("LOGIN.DEMO_DOCTOR")</li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - @T("LOGIN.DEMO_USER")</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 13: After a failure, the controller returns this page with the username already entered;
  • line 20: a standard HTML form: the browser submits the username, password, and CAPTCHA answer on its own;
  • lines 23–29: [autofocus] is a Boolean attribute: only one of the two fields receives it. The cursor is placed in the username field, or in the password field if the username is already known. The values of [autocomplete] ([username], [current-password]) assist the browsers’ password managers;
  • line 32: the CAPTCHA; the second argument provides the partial view template;
  • lines 45–46: the second button submits the same form to [/register/access] (attribute [formaction], see Example 20): the server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page. [formnovalidate]: the browser does not require a username and password, as they are not needed to create an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first button on the form: “Log in”;
  • lines 51–56: demo accounts (password = username).

docs.title: 11.17.2.2. Views/Schedule/Schedule.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Schedule/Schedule.cshtml - the main page (see ScheduleController).
   Three blocks, like the three components of the Angular client:
     1. the choice of the doctor and the day  (<app-doctor-day-picker>)
     2. the schedule                          (<app-agenda>)
     3. the booking dialog                    (<app-booking-dialog>)
   A possible error (invalid date, unknown doctor) is displayed at the
   bottom of the page by the layout (see Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml).
   ========================================================================= *@
@model ScheduleModel

@* 1. choice of the doctor and the day: a GET form, which simply
   reloads this page with ?doctorId=...&day=... in the URL *@
<form method="get" action="/schedule" class="card p-3 mb-3">
  <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
    <div class="col-sm-5">
      <label class="form-label" for="doctorId">@T("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL")</label>
      <select id="doctorId" name="doctorId" class="form-select" required>
        <option value="">@T("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR")</option>
        @foreach (var doctor in Model.Doctors)
        {
          <option value="@doctor.Id" selected="@doctor.Selected">@doctor.Label</option>
        }
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-4">
      <label class="form-label" for="day">@T("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL")</label>
      <input id="day" name="day" type="date" class="form-control" value="@Model.Day" required>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-3">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">@T("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_SCHEDULE")</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</form>

@* patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no "Book" button *@
@if (Model.Info is not null)
{
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    @T(Model.Info) <a href="/my-area" class="alert-link">@T("APP.MENU_MY_AREA")</a>
  </div>
}

@* 2. the schedule *@
@if (Model.Schedule is { } schedule)
{
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>@T("SCHEDULE.TITLE_PREFIX") @schedule.Day - @schedule.Doctor</h5>

    @if (schedule.Rows.Count > 0)
    {
      <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>@T("SCHEDULE.COLUMN_SLOT")</th>
            <th>@T("SCHEDULE.COLUMN_STATUS")</th>
            <th></th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          @foreach (var row in schedule.Rows)
          {
            <tr class="@(row.Bookable ? "free-slot" : null)">
              <td>@row.Time</td>
              <td>
                @* [Patient] is filled only if the user is allowed to
                   see this name (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient for THEIR
                   appointment) - otherwise, simply "Booked" *@
                @if (row.Free)
                {
                  <span class="badge text-bg-success">@T("SCHEDULE.FREE")</span>
                }
                else if (row.Patient is not null)
                {
                  <span class="badge @(row.Mine ? "text-bg-primary" : "text-bg-secondary")">@row.Patient</span>
                }
                else
                {
                  <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">@T("SCHEDULE.BOOKED_BY_OTHER")</span>
                }
              </td>
              <td>
                @* the displayed buttons have been decided by the controller
                   (Bookable, AppointmentId) according to the role of the user *@
                @if (row.Bookable)
                {
                  @* "Book" is a simple link: it reopens this page
                     with the booking dialog of this slot *@
                  <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="@row.BookUrl">@T("SCHEDULE.BOOK")</a>
                }
                @if (row.AppointmentId is not null)
                {
                  @* "Cancel" MODIFIES data: it is therefore a POST *@
                  <form method="post" action="/schedule/cancel" class="m-0"
                        data-confirmation="@T("SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM")">
                    <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="@row.AppointmentId">
                    <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="@Model.DoctorId">
                    <input type="hidden" name="day" value="@Model.Day">
                    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">@T("SCHEDULE.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT")</button>
                  </form>
                }
              </td>
            </tr>
          }
        </tbody>
      </table>
    }
    else
    {
      <p class="text-muted mb-0">@T("SCHEDULE.NO_SLOTS")</p>
    }
  </div>
}
else
{
  <p class="text-muted">@T("SCHEDULE.EMPTY_STATE")</p>
}

@* 3. the booking dialog, only if the URL contains &book=... *@
@if (Model.Booking is not null)
{
  @await Html.PartialAsync("_Booking", Model)
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 14–34: selecting the doctor and the day: a GET form (see Example 17), which reloads the page with [?doctorId=...&day=...] in the URL. Each doctor is a [OptionView] that indicates whether they are selected. A [type="date"] field sends the date in [yyyy-mm-dd] format (see Example 18);
  • lines 37–42: a message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment: it explains why the “Book” buttons are missing;
  • line 45: the calendar, if requested. The condition [is { } schedule] checks that the property is not [null] and stores its value in the variable [schedule];
  • line 48: the title: “Schedule for 2026-09-25 – Mme Marie PELISSIER”;
  • line 63: a bookable time slot changes color on hover (class [free-slot], see [styles.css]). When an attribute’s value is [null], [Razor] does not write the attribute at all: the other lines do not have the [class] attribute;
  • Lines 69–80: three cases: available; booked, with the patient’s name (in blue if it is the logged-in patient’s appointment, [Mine]); booked with no visible name, “Booked.” The controller only populates [Patient] if the user has permission to view that name;
  • Lines 85–90: “Book” is a link: it reopens this page, displaying the reservation window for this time slot ([BookUrl], prepared by the controller);
  • lines 91–101: “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form, with confirmation ([data-confirmation], see Example 21). The hidden fields [doctorId] and [day] allow the controller to redirect to the same calendar. In the loop, [Model] always refers to the page template: there is no need for the equivalent of [@root] or [Handlebars];
  • lines 110 and 116: a doctor with no available time slots, or no calendar has been requested yet;
  • lines 120–123: the booking window, if the controller has prepared it.

  • Lines 26–45: one line per person, with two buttons;

docs.title: 11.17.2.4. Views/Persons/Form.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Persons/Form.cshtml - creation OR update of a doctor
   or of a client (ADMIN). Model.Creating distinguishes the two cases.

   When the input is refused (empty field, login already taken...), the
   controller sends back THIS view with:
     - the values already typed (Model.Values);
     - the faulty fields outlined in red (Bootstrap "is-invalid" class);
     - under a field refused by the validation, its message;
     - the error message of the page, displayed AT THE BOTTOM of the page by the
       layout (see Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml).
   ========================================================================= *@
@model PersonFormModel
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">@T(Model.PageTitle)</h5>

      @* novalidate: we let the SERVER validate (it is the one that has authority);
         the browser checks (required...) are only a convenience,
         which a user can always bypass *@
      <form method="post" action="@Model.Action" novalidate>
        @if (!Model.Creating)
        {
          <input type="hidden" name="version" value="@Model.Values.Version">
        }

        @* title, first name, last name: partial common to three forms *@
        @await Html.PartialAsync("_PersonFields", Model)

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">@T("PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION")</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">@T("PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="off"
                 class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("login")" value="@Model.Values.Login">
          @if (Model.ErrorOf("login") is { } loginError)
          {
            <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(loginError)</div>
          }
          else
          {
            <div class="form-text">@T(Model.Creating ? "PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_CREATE" : "PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_EDIT")</div>
          }
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">@T("PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL")</label>
          @* never pre-filled: the password never goes back to the browser *@
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                 class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("password")">
          @if (Model.ErrorOf("password") is { } passwordError)
          {
            <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(passwordError)</div>
          }
          else
          {
            <div class="form-text">@T(Model.Creating ? "PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_CREATE" : "PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT")</div>
          }
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">@T("PERSONS.SAVE")</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="@Model.ListUrl">@T("PERSONS.BACK")</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 17: The title (“Add a doctor,” “Edit a patient,” etc.) is the page title key, provided by the controller;
  • line 22: The URL is provided by the controller: the same view is used for both adding and editing doctors and clients. [novalidate]: The server handles validation (see Example 19);
  • lines 23–25: for an edit, the record version, in a hidden field: this is the optimistic lock from Example 28;
  • line 29: the identity fields;
  • lines 34–44: the login, with an error message or, if none, a help text. The help text differs depending on whether it is an addition (“Optional: defaults to the last name in lower case.”) or an edit;
  • lines 48–59: the password, which is never pre-filled; it is never sent back to the browser. [autocomplete="new-password"]: the browser does not suggest the administrator’s saved password. The length is limited to 72 characters because the [bcrypt] algorithm ignores the following characters;
  • Line 64: The link back to the list is a hyperlink.

docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/Registration/Registration.cshtml - "Create a patient account" (public
   page, see RegistrationController). Same identity fields as the
   ADMIN's form (_PersonFields partial), but the login and the
   password are required, with confirmation.
   No captcha HERE: this page is only reached after copying
   the one of the authentication page ("Create a patient account" button).
   ========================================================================= *@
@model RegistrationModel
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-1">@T("REGISTRATION.TITLE")</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small mb-3">@T("REGISTRATION.INTRO")</p>

      <form method="post" action="/register" novalidate>
        @await Html.PartialAsync("_PersonFields", Model)

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">@T("PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION")</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">@T("PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("login")" value="@Model.Values.Login">
          @if (Model.ErrorOf("login") is { } loginError)
          {
            <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(loginError)</div>
          }
          else
          {
            <div class="form-text">@T("REGISTRATION.LOGIN_HELP")</div>
          }
        </div>

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="password">@T("PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL")</label>
            <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("password")">
            @if (Model.ErrorOf("password") is { } passwordError)
            {
              <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(passwordError, ("min", Model.PasswordMin))</div>
            }
            else
            {
              <div class="form-text">@T("REGISTRATION.PASSWORD_HELP", ("min", Model.PasswordMin))</div>
            }
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">@T("ACCOUNT.CONFIRMATION_LABEL")</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("confirmation")">
            @if (Model.ErrorOf("confirmation") is { } confirmationError)
            {
              <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(confirmationError)</div>
            }
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">@T("REGISTRATION.SUBMIT")</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/login">@T("REGISTRATION.BACK_TO_LOGIN")</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Creating a customer account, public page. No CAPTCHA here: you can only reach this page after entering the CAPTCHA from the login page.

  • line 17: the same identity fields as the form on ADMIN;
  • Lines 22–32: the username, which is required this time;
  • lines 37–47: the help text and the “too short” message have a parameter, [{min}], which is the minimum password length provided by the template ([PasswordMin]). A message without the parameter [{min}] simply ignores the provided value;
  • lines 50–56: password confirmation;
  • line 62: return to the login page.

docs.title: 11.17.2.6. Views/PatientArea/Area.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================
   Views/PatientArea/Area.cshtml - "My area": the home page of the
   patient (USER role), displayed right after logging in.
     - two options: [Manage my account] and [View a schedule];
     - their upcoming appointment, if they have one, with the means to cancel it.
   ========================================================================= *@
@model AreaModel
<h4 class="mb-3">@T("AREA.HELLO", ("name", Model.Patient))</h4>

<div class="row g-3 mb-4">
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="/my-account">
      <h5 class="mb-1">@T("AREA.MANAGE_ACCOUNT")</h5>
      <span class="text-muted">@T("AREA.MANAGE_ACCOUNT_HELP")</span>

</div>

<div class="card p-3">
  <h5>@T("AREA.MY_APPOINTMENT")</h5>

  {
    @* normally only one (rule "one upcoming appointment at a time"),
       but the page can display several *@

    {

          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger">@T("AREA.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT")</button>
        </form>
      </div>
    }
  }
  else
  {
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">@T("AREA.NO_APPOINTMENT")</p>
  }
</div>
  • line 8: “Hello Mr Jean MARTIN”;
  • lines 12–21: both options are links, displayed as cards (class [option-card], see [styles.css]);
  • lines 31–46: upcoming appointments (usually just one). Within a [@if] block, the format is [C#]: the [for] loop is written without [@]. A border ([border-bottom]) separates the appointments, except after the last one;
  • lines 40–44: the cancellation, a POST form with confirmation.

docs.title: 11.17.2.7. Views/PatientArea/Account.cshtml
docs.text:
@* =========================================================================

   Two independent forms on the same page:
     1. the update (identity, login, optional new password);
     2. the deletion of the account - which also cancels its appointments.

   ========================================================================= *@
@model MyAccountModel

    @* 1. update *@
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">

        <input type="hidden" name="version" value="@Model.Values.Version">

        @await Html.PartialAsync("_PersonFields", Model)

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">@T("PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION")</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">@T("PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("login")" value="@Model.Values.Login">
          @if (Model.ErrorOf("login") is { } loginError)
          {
            <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(loginError)</div>
          }
        </div>

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="password">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.NEW_PASSWORD_LABEL")</label>
            <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                   class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("password")">
            @if (Model.ErrorOf("password") is { } passwordError)
            {
              <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(passwordError, ("min", Model.PasswordMin))</div>
            }
            else
            {
              <div class="form-text">@T("PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT")</div>
            }
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">@T("ACCOUNT.CONFIRMATION_LABEL")</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                   class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("confirmation")">
            @if (Model.ErrorOf("confirmation") is { } confirmationError)
            {
              <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(confirmationError)</div>
            }
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="currentPassword">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="currentPassword" name="currentPassword" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="current-password" required
                 class="form-control @Model.InvalidClass("currentPassword")">
          @if (Model.ErrorOf("currentPassword") is { } currentError)
          {
            <div class="invalid-feedback">@T(currentError)</div>
          }
          else
          {
            <div class="form-text">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_HELP")</div>
          }
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">@T("PERSONS.SAVE")</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/my-area">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.BACK")</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    @* 2. deletion *@
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_TITLE")</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_HELP")</p>
      <form method="post" action="/my-account/delete" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="@T("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_CONFIRM")">
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="deletePassword">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL")</label>
          <input id="deletePassword" name="deletePassword" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">@T("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_SUBMIT")</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
  • lines 16–76: account modification: identity, login, new password (optional), and its confirmation;
  • line 17: the version of the customer record (optimistic lock);
  • lines 59–69: the current password, required for any changes;
  • Lines 83–91: Deletion, with confirmation. Two independent forms on the same page: each submits only its own fields. The password field therefore has a different name here ([deletePassword]) and a different identifier. This form does not have the [novalidate] attribute: the browser requires the password ([required]) even before triggering the [submit] event—that is, before asking the confirmation question.

docs.text: The [wwwroot] folder is served by [UseStaticFiles] (see Example 15). The [wwwroot/lib/bootstrap] folder contains [Bootstrap] (its stylesheet [css/bootstrap.min.css] and its license), which are not displayed.

docs.title: 11.19.1. wwwroot/css/styles.css
docs.text:
/* =========================================================================
   wwwroot/css/styles.css - a few settings on top of Bootstrap
   (taken from src/styles.css of the Angular client, via the NestJS project).
   ========================================================================= */

body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   .error-zone: the error messages, at the bottom of the page, on a light pink background
   (see Views/Shared/_Errors.cshtml).
   position: sticky + bottom: if the page is taller than the window (a

   window instead of disappearing below the fold - without ever
   covering the content when the page is short.
   z-index: above the grey background of the booking dialog (.modal-backdrop).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.error-zone {

  bottom: 1rem;
  z-index: 1060;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef; /* light pink */
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

/* the two big options of the patient's "My area" page */

  transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}

.option-card:hover {
  border-color: #0d6efd;
  box-shadow: 0 0.25rem 0.75rem rgba(13, 110, 253, 0.15);
