    [Required(ErrorMessage = "The password is required.")]
    [MinLength(6, ErrorMessage = "The password must have at least 6 characters.")]
    public string? Password { get; set; }

    // a rule about TWO fields: [Compare] compares with Password
    [Compare(nameof(Password), ErrorMessage = "The confirmation does not match the password.")]
    public string? Confirmation { get; set; }
}

// the view model: the values to display again, the errors per field
public class RegistrationForm
{
    public RegistrationModel Values { get; init; } = new();
    public Dictionary<string, string> Errors { get; init; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
    public bool Html5 { get; init; }
}

// the model of the _Field partial view: an input field
public record FieldModel(string Name, string Label, string Type, string? Value, string? Error, string Attributes);

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 9–16: a property with a private field. Its accessor, [set]—called by the model binding—removes unnecessary spaces from the input: [" Martin "] becomes ["Martin"]. A name consisting solely of spaces is converted to [null] by the model binding itself, and [[Required]] is rejected;
  • line 12: [[MaxLength]] limits the length of a string, just like [[StringLength]];
  • Lines 25–26: The age is converted to an integer and then validated;
  • line 29: at least 6 characters;
  • line 33: the rule “the confirmation matches the password” applies to two fields. The [[Compare]] attribute compares the property it decorates to another property, designated by its name ([nameof(Password)]: the property name, verified by the compiler);
  • lines 38–42: the view template: the values to be redisplayed, errors sorted by field (a dictionary whose keys are case-insensitive), and a Boolean explained further on;
  • line 46: the partial view template that displays a field.

The file [Controllers/RegistrationController.cs]:

using Example19.Models;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Example19.Controllers;

[Route("register")]
public class RegistrationController : Controller
{
    // ?html5=1: we let the browser validate the form before sending it
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Display(bool html5)
    {
        return View("Registration", new RegistrationForm { Html5 = html5 });
    }

    [HttpPost("")]
    public IActionResult Register(RegistrationModel input, [FromQuery] bool html5)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            // the errors per field, to display each message under its field
            var errors = ModelState
                .Where(c => c.Value!.Errors.Count > 0)
                .ToDictionary(c => c.Key, c => c.Value!.Errors[0].ErrorMessage, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
            // we display the form AGAIN: typed values (except the passwords),
            // and a message under each invalid field
            input.Password = input.Confirmation = null;
            ViewData["Error"] = "The form contains errors.";
            return View("Registration", new RegistrationForm { Values = input, Errors = errors, Html5 = html5 });
        }
        return View("Welcome", input);
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 11–13: the empty form. The parameter [html5] will be explained later;
  • Line 17: The template link populates [input] using the form fields and validates it. [[FromQuery]] retrieves [html5] from URL;
  • Lines 19–24: If there are errors, they are organized by field. A field may violate multiple constraints: only the first error message ([Errors[0]]) is retained;
  • lines 27–29: The form is redisplayed: the entered values (except passwords), errors by field, and a general message, stored in [ViewData] for the template;
  • line 31: otherwise, the welcome page, with the converted values (age is a number, the name has been cleaned up).

A conversion error (an age [abc]) generates an English message by default: [The value 'abc' is not valid for Age.] (see example 08). The file [Program.cs] replaces it:

using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using System.Text.Unicode;
using Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews(options =>
{
    // the messages of the CONVERSION errors (e.g. age "abc"), replacing the default ones
    var messages = options.ModelBindingMessageProvider;
    messages.SetAttemptedValueIsInvalidAccessor((value, field) => $"The value [{value}] is not valid.");
    messages.SetValueMustNotBeNullAccessor(field => "This field is required.");
});
// Razor writes accented characters as is (and not "é");
// < > & " ' remain escaped
builder.Services.AddSingleton(HtmlEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All));

var app = builder.Build();

// 1. the static files of the wwwroot folder: wwwroot/css/styles.css is served as /css/styles.css
app.UseStaticFiles();
// 2. Bootstrap, shared by the examples: the examples/common/bootstrap folder is served under /bootstrap
app.UseStaticFiles(new StaticFileOptions
{
    FileProvider = new PhysicalFileProvider(Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(builder.Environment.ContentRootPath, "..", "common", "bootstrap"))),
    RequestPath = "/bootstrap",
});

app.MapControllers();
app.Run();
  • Lines 6–11: The messages for template-linking errors are provided by the [ModelBindingMessageProvider] object from the options of MVC. Each method in [Set...Accessor] replaces one of these with a function that generates the message. [SetAttemptedValueIsInvalidAccessor] handles a value that cannot be converted; it receives the value and the field name. The case study thus replaces all of these messages.

The fields are all built using the same model: a partial view factors them out. The file [Views/Shared/_Field.cshtml]:

@* an input field; its model: name, label, type, value, error, and the
   HTML5 validation attributes (required, maxlength...) *@
@model FieldModel
<div class="mb-2">
  <label class="form-label" for="@Model.Name">@Model.Label</label>
  <input class="form-control @(Model.Error is null ? "" : "is-invalid")" id="@Model.Name" name="@Model.Name"
         type="@Model.Type" value="@Model.Value" @Html.Raw(Model.Attributes)>
  @if (Model.Error is not null)
  {
    <div class="invalid-feedback">@Model.Error</div>
  }
</div>
  • line 6: the class [Bootstrap] [is-invalid] highlights an invalid field in red;
  • line 7: the validation attributes HTML5 are passed as parameters and inserted without escaping ([Html.Raw]): they are written by the developer, not entered by the user;
  • line 10: the error message, below the field (class [Bootstrap] [invalid-feedback]).

The file [Views/Registration/Registration.cshtml]:

@model RegistrationForm
@{
    // the error of a field, or null
    string? Error(string field) => Model.Errors.GetValueOrDefault(field);
}
<h1 class="h3">Registration</h1>
@if (Model.Html5)
{
  <p>Browser validation <b>enabled</b> - <a href="/register">disable it</a></p>
}
else
{
  <p>Browser validation <b>disabled</b> - <a href="/register?html5=true">enable it</a></p>
}
@* novalidate: the browser ignores the required, min... attributes and
   sends the form as is; only the server validates *@
<form method="post" action="/register@(Model.Html5 ? "?html5=true" : "")" novalidate="@(!Model.Html5)">
  <partial name="_Field" model='new FieldModel("name", "Name", "text", Model.Values.Name, Error("name"), "required maxlength=\"20\"")' />
  <partial name="_Field" model='new FieldModel("email", "Email address", "email", Model.Values.Email, Error("email"), "required")' />
  <partial name="_Field" model='new FieldModel("age", "Age", "number", Model.Values.Age?.ToString(), Error("age"), "required min=\"18\" max=\"120\"")' />
  <partial name="_Field" model='new FieldModel("password", "Password", "password", null, Error("password"), "required minlength=\"6\"")' />
  <partial name="_Field" model='new FieldModel("confirmation", "Confirmation", "password", null, Error("confirmation"), "required")' />
  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Register</button>
</form>
  • line 4: a local function [C#], declared in the block [@{ }]: it returns the error for a field, or [null];
  • line 17: the Boolean attribute [novalidate] is set when [Html5] is false;
  • Lines 18–22: Each field is an insertion from the partial view, using a template generated on the fly.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Registration</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
    @RenderBody()
    @* the global error, at the bottom of the page, on a light pink background;
       ViewData["Error"] is set by the action *@
    @if (ViewData["Error"] is string error)
    {
      <div class="error-area" role="alert">@error</div>
    }
  </div>
</body>
</html>
  • lines 14–16: the global message is displayed at the bottom of the page on a light pink background (class [error-area] derived from [wwwroot/css/styles.css]), as in the case study. [is string error] checks the value's type and stores it in a variable.

Let’s submit the form (http://localhost:5000/register) with several errors:

then correctly filled out (with spaces around the name):

docs.title: 4.7.1. Validation by the browser
docs.text:
The attributes [required], [maxlength], [min], [max], [type="email"]... instruct the browser to validate the form before submitting it: the user is immediately notified via a tooltip, without any round-trip communication with the server. This is the behavior achieved by clicking the “enable it” link (http://localhost:5000/register?html5=true), which removes the [novalidate] attribute from the form.

This validation is a convenience, not a security measure: you can bypass it simply by removing the [required] attribute using the browser’s developer tools, or by sending the request with [curl]. Server-side validation remains essential. That’s why the example disables browser validation by default: to demonstrate how the server works. The case study, however, retains both: the HTML5 attribute for convenience, and server-side validation for security.

docs.title: 4.8. Example 20: The Post/Redirect/Get Pattern
docs.text:
When a POST form submits successfully, the action can display a page directly. The problem arises if the user then refreshes that page (F5 key): the browser resubmits the form, and the operation is performed a second time (an order placed twice, an appointment made twice...). The Post / Redirect / Get pattern (PRG) prevents this problem: a successful POST action does not generate a page; instead, it redirects to a GET page. Reloading this page simply triggers another GET, with no effect.

One detail remains: the GET page must display a message (“the task has been added”), even though this message was generated by the POST action in a different request. To address this, [ASP.NET Core] provides [TempData]: a dictionary whose contents persist until the next request and disappear as soon as they are read. It is a flash message. By default, [TempData] is stored in a cookie, encrypted by the server.

The file [Services/TasksService.cs]:

namespace Example20.Services;

// the task list, in memory, shared by everyone (singleton)
public class TasksService
{
    private readonly List<string> tasks = ["Read chapter 3"];

    public IReadOnlyList<string> List() => tasks;

    public void Add(string label) => tasks.Add(label);
}

The [Controllers/TasksController.cs] file:

using Example20.Services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Example20.Controllers;

[Route("tasks")]
public class TasksController(TasksService tasks) : Controller
{
    // GET /tasks: the list and the add form
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult Display()
    {
        return View("Tasks", tasks.List());
    }

    // POST /tasks: the Post / Redirect / Get pattern
    [HttpPost("")]
    public IActionResult Add(string? label)
    {
        var text = (label ?? "").Trim();
        if (text == "" || text.Length > 40)
        {
            // invalid input: we display the page again, without a redirect
            ViewData["Label"] = label;
            ViewData["Error"] = "The label must have 1 to 40 characters.";
            return View("Tasks", tasks.List());
        }
        tasks.Add(text);
        // TempData: a message that will survive the redirect, for the NEXT request
        TempData["Flash"] = $"The task [{text}] has been added.";
        // no page: a redirect to the GET page
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(Display));
    }

    // POST /tasks/without-prg: the counter-example (a page in response to the POST)
    [HttpPost("without-prg")]
    public IActionResult AddWithoutPrg(string? label)
    {
        tasks.Add(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(label) ? "(untitled)" : label.Trim());
        ViewData["WithoutPrg"] = true;
        return View("Tasks", tasks.List());
    }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • lines 11–13: the list page;
  • lines 21–26: an invalid entry: the page is reloaded (no redirection—the entry and error message must be retained);
  • lines 28–32: a valid input: the operation, the message flashes in [TempData], then a 302 redirect to the [Display] action. [RedirectToAction] calculates the URL for the action based on its route (see Example 04). [nameof(Display)] is the method name, which is validated by the compiler;
  • lines 36–41: the counterexample, for comparison.

The file [Views/Tasks/Tasks.cshtml]:

@model IReadOnlyList<string>
<h1 class="h3">My tasks</h1>
<ol>
  @foreach (var task in Model)
  {
    <li>@task</li>
  }
</ol>
<form method="post" action="/tasks" class="d-flex gap-2">
  <input class="form-control" name="label" value="@ViewData["Label"]" placeholder="New task">
  <button class="btn btn-primary text-nowrap" type="submit">Add</button>
  @* formaction: this button sends the SAME form to another address *@
  <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary text-nowrap" type="submit" formaction="/tasks/without-prg">Add without PRG</button>
</form>
@if (ViewData["WithoutPrg"] is true)
{
  <p class="text-danger mt-2">Page displayed in response to a POST: press F5 and the task will be added a second time.</p>
}
  • line 13: the [formaction] attribute of a button submits the form to a different address than the one specified by the form’s [action] attribute. The form thus has two buttons, which trigger two different actions. The case study uses this approach on its login page.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Tasks</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
    @* the flash message, at the top of the page: READING it removes it from TempData *@
    @if (TempData["Flash"] is string flash)
    {
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">@flash</div>
    }
    @RenderBody()
    @if (ViewData["Error"] is string error)
    {
      <div class="error-area" role="alert">@error</div>
    }
  </div>
</body>
</html>

The flash message is displayed at the top of the page (lines 12–14), and the error message at the bottom (lines 17–19). Reading [TempData["Flash"]] marks the value as consumed: it is cleared at the end of the request.

Here is what [curl] sees when the form is successfully submitted. The [-c file] option saves the received cookies, [-b file] sends them back; [--data-urlencode] encodes spaces and accents in the field:

curl -i -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt --data-urlencode "label=Review ASP.NET" http://localhost:5000/tasks

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Content-Length: 0
Location: /tasks
Set-Cookie: .AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider=CfDJ8Mr17zLSwO9AhYlPOJdkD8mjtY...; path=/; samesite=lax; httponly

The response is a redirect, with the cookie [.AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider], which contains the encrypted flash message (its value, which is very long, has been truncated). The next request sends the cookie; the response deletes it (expiration date in the past):

curl -i -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt http://localhost:5000/tasks

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Set-Cookie: .AspNetCore.Mvc.CookieTempDataProvider=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; path=/; samesite=lax; httponly

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Tasks</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 36rem">
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">The task [Review ASP.NET] has been added.</div>
    <h1 class="h3">My tasks</h1>
<ol>
    <li>Read chapter 3</li>
    <li>Review ASP.NET</li>
</ol>
<form method="post" action="/tasks" class="d-flex gap-2">
  <input class="form-control" name="label" placeholder="New task">
  <button class="btn btn-primary text-nowrap" type="submit">Add</button>
  <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary text-nowrap" type="submit" formaction="/tasks/without-prg">Add without PRG</button>
</form>

  </div>
</body>
</html>

In the browser (http://localhost:5000/tasks), after adding a task:

The address bar displays [/tasks]: this is the page GET. You can safely reload it; the message disappears. An empty entry:

And the counterexample:

Here, reloading the page triggers a browser warning (“Confirm form submission”), then adds the task a second time. All POST forms in the case study follow the PRG pattern.

docs.title: 4.9. Example 21: Links, Buttons, and Confirmation
docs.text:
A simple rule guides the choice between a link and a button:

  • a link ([<a href>]) generates a GET request. A GET request must not modify anything: browsers, search engines, and antivirus programs may follow links on their own to prepare or analyze a page;
  • an operation that modifies data (add, edit, delete, log out) is a button in a form POST.

Example 21 manages a list of contacts: you can view a contact by clicking a link and delete it by clicking a button, which opens a confirmation window. The files for this example:

21-links-buttons/
├── Controllers/
│   └── ContactsController.cs
├── Services/
│   └── ContactsService.cs
├── Views/
│   ├── Contacts/
│   │   ├── Details.cshtml
│   │   └── List.cshtml
│   ├── Shared/
│   │   ├── _Confirmation.cshtml
│   │   └── _Layout.cshtml
│   ├── _ViewImports.cshtml
│   └── _ViewStart.cshtml
├── wwwroot/
│   ├── css/
│   │   └── styles.css
│   └── js/
│       └── app.js
├── appsettings.json
├── Example21.csproj
└── Program.cs

The [Services/ContactsService.cs] file:

namespace Example21.Services;

// a contact: an identifier, a name, a phone number
public record Contact(int Id, string Name, string Phone);

// the contacts, in memory, shared by everyone (singleton)
public class ContactsService
{
    private readonly List<Contact> contacts =
    [
        new(1, "Marie Durand", "01 23 45 67 89"),
        new(2, "Paul Martin", "06 12 34 56 78"),
        new(3, "Philippe Jandot", "02 98 76 54 32"),
    ];
    private int lastId = 3;

    public IReadOnlyList<Contact> List() => contacts;

    // null if the contact does not exist
    public Contact? Read(int id) => contacts.Find(c => c.Id == id);

    public Contact? Edit(int id, string name, string phone)
    {
        var index = contacts.FindIndex(c => c.Id == id);
        if (index < 0) return null;
        // a record is immutable: we replace it with a modified copy (with)
        contacts[index] = contacts[index] with { Name = name, Phone = phone };
        return contacts[index];
    }

    public Contact Add(string name, string phone)
    {
        var contact = new Contact(++lastId, name, phone);
        contacts.Add(contact);
        return contact;
    }

    public Contact? Delete(int id)
    {
        var contact = Read(id);
        if (contact is not null) contacts.Remove(contact);
        return contact;
    }
}
  • Line 4: a contact;
  • line 20: [Find] returns [null] if no contact has that ID;
  • lines 22–28: a [record] is immutable: its properties are not modified; instead, it is replaced with a modified copy. The expression [with { ... }] creates this copy;
  • lines 31–35: [++lastId] increments the counter before using it: the identifiers are 4, 5...

The file [Controllers/ContactsController.cs]:

using Example21.Services;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Example21.Controllers;

[Route("contacts")]
public class ContactsController(ContactsService contacts) : Controller
{
    // a LINK (<a href>): a GET request, which modifies nothing
    [HttpGet("")]
    public IActionResult List()
    {
        return View(contacts.List());
    }

    [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
    public IActionResult Details(int id)
    {
        var contact = contacts.Read(id);
        return contact is null ? NotFound() : View(contact);
    }

    // a BUTTON in a POST form: a request that modifies data
    [HttpPost("{id:int}")]
    public IActionResult Save(int id, string name, string phone)
    {
        var contact = contacts.Edit(id, name, phone);
        if (contact is null) return NotFound();
        TempData["Flash"] = $"The contact [{contact.Name}] has been edited.";
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(List));
    }

    // same form, another button (formaction attribute): another action
    [HttpPost("{id:int}/duplicate")]
    public IActionResult Duplicate(int id, string name, string phone)
    {
        var copy = contacts.Add($"{name} (copy)", phone);
        TempData["Flash"] = $"The contact [{copy.Name}] has been created.";
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(List));
    }

    [HttpPost("{id:int}/delete")]
    public IActionResult Delete(int id)
    {
        var contact = contacts.Delete(id);
        if (contact is null) return NotFound();
        TempData["Flash"] = $"The contact [{contact.Name}] has been deleted.";
        return RedirectToAction(nameof(List));
    }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 11–20: the two pages: the list and the contact detail page. The route constraint [:int] (see Example 02) only accepts an integer identifier; a nonexistent contact results in a 404 error;
  • lines 24–30: saving a record, using PRG;
  • lines 34–39: duplication, triggered by a second button on the same form (attribute [formaction]);
  • lines 42–48: deletion, using POST.

The file [Views/Contacts/List.cshtml]:

@model IReadOnlyList<Contact>
<h1 class="h3">Contacts</h1>
<table class="table align-middle">
  <tbody>
    @foreach (var contact in Model)
    {
      <tr>
        <td>@contact.Name</td>
        <td>@contact.Phone</td>
        <td class="text-end">
          @* view: a simple link *@
          <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" href="/contacts/@contact.Id">View</a>
          @* delete: a POST form, whose submission will be confirmed *@
          <form method="post" action="/contacts/@contact.Id/delete" class="d-inline"
                data-confirmation="Delete the contact @contact.Name?">
            <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" type="submit">Delete</button>
          </form>
        </td>
      </tr>
    }
  </tbody>
</table>
  • line 12: view: a link, displayed as a button by [Bootstrap];
  • lines 14–17: delete: a small form (POST), reduced to its button. The [data-confirmation] attribute contains the question to be asked before submission. The [data-*] attributes are optional: HTML ignores them, while [JavaScript] on the page can read them.

The [Views/Contacts/Details.cshtml] file:

docs.title: 4.9.1. The confirmation window
docs.text:
The browser dialog box ([window.confirm]) cannot be formatted or translated: its buttons remain in the browser’s language. It is replaced by a [Bootstrap] window, embedded in the page and hidden until needed. The [Views/Shared/_Confirmation.cshtml] file:

@* a single window for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first *@
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title">Confirmation</h5>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">No, go back</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">Yes, confirm</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 2: the [d-none] class hides the window;
  • line 3: the gray background;
  • line 11: the question’s position;
  • lines 14–15: the two buttons, identified by the [data-action] attribute.

The file [Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Contacts</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3" style="max-width: 40rem">
    @if (TempData["Flash"] is string flash)
    {
      <div class="alert alert-success" role="status">@flash</div>
    }
    @RenderBody()
  </div>
  @* the confirmation window, present in every page *@
  <partial name="_Confirmation" />
  @* the script, at the end of the page: the elements it looks for already exist *@
  <script src="/js/app.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • line 18: the window is present on all pages;
  • line 20: the script is loaded at the bottom of the page; when it runs, the elements it looks for already exist. It is served by [UseStaticFiles] from [wwwroot/js/app.js].

A small portion of [JavaScript] links the forms to the window. The file [wwwroot/js/app.js]:

// confirmation of the forms that carry the data-confirmation="..." attribute
// Without JavaScript, these forms are simply sent without confirmation.
(() => {
  const modal = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal');
  const message = document.getElementById('confirmation-modal-message');
  let pending = null; // the form to send if the user confirms

  // 1. we intercept the submission of the forms to confirm
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((form) => {
    form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
      event.preventDefault(); // the submission is suspended
      pending = form;
      message.textContent = form.dataset.confirmation;
      modal.classList.remove('d-none'); // the window appears
    });
  });

  // 2. the two buttons of the window
  modal.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
    const action = event.target.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'yes') {
      pending.submit(); // submission, WITHOUT firing the 'submit' event again
    } else if (action === 'no') {
      modal.classList.add('d-none');
      pending = null;
    }
  });
})();
  • line 3: the code is wrapped in a function that executes immediately, to avoid creating global variables;
  • lines 9–14: the submission of each form bearing the attribute [data-confirmation] is intercepted. [preventDefault()] suspends the submission; the form is stored, the question is placed in the window ([textContent], not [innerHTML]: the question is displayed as text, never interpreted as HTML), and the window is displayed;
  • Lines 19–25: “Yes” submits the cached form. The [submit()] method of a form submits it without triggering the [submit] event: there is no new confirmation prompt. “No” hides the window.

If [JavaScript] is disabled, the forms simply submit without confirmation: the application still works. This is the principle of incremental improvement: [JavaScript] adds convenience, but it is not essential. The case study follows this principle (its script, [wwwroot/js/app.js], adds keyboard handling: the Esc key and focus). The resulting pages, generated from http://localhost:5000/contacts: the list, the confirmation prompt, the list after deletion, and a contact’s profile:

Finally, we verify that deletion cannot be triggered by a query GET:

curl -i http://localhost:5000/contacts/2/delete

HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Content-Length: 0
Allow: POST

The path exists, but not for the GET method: [ASP.NET Core] returns [405 Method Not Allowed], and the [Allow] header indicates the accepted method. With POST:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:5000/contacts/2/delete

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Content-Length: 0
Location: /contacts
